title: Offensive line grades for the Cowboys first preseason game
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are set with their offensive line starters, which is why none of this group played on Saturday. The main five: LT – Tyler Guyton LG – Tyler Smith C – Cooper Beebe RG – Tyler Booker RT – Terence Steele Now, the attention shifts to finding quality backups to build the depth […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys are set with their offensive line starters, which is why none of this group played on Saturday. The main five: LT – Tyler Guyton LG – Tyler Smith C – Cooper Beebe RG – Tyler Booker RT – Terence Steele Now, the attention shifts to finding quality backups to build the depth chart so they are prepared when the inevitable injury bug rears its ugly head. The team got a good look at the backups against Seattle with a mixture of results. Here are the performances of the team’s key backups and an updated job security update for each player. T.J. Bass A once undrafted free agent out of Oregon, Bass is now the senior staff member in terms of team service among the Cowboys’ main linemen reserves. He’s taken over the backup center responsibilities from Brock Hoffman and will become the first player the coaches call on if an interior player gets hurt. Preseason game grade: B+ Against the Seahawks, Bass handled himself well. He started at center and showed he is the second team’s most tried and trusted blocker, moving well and keeping the pocket clean for Sam Howell. He only played seven snaps coming out of the game midway through the second series, but on almost every rep, he locked up with his man and completely neutralized him. His balance and strength were on full display. Roster security: Locked in as the team’s top interior piece. Nate Thomas A late-round pick in 2024, Thomas is now entering his third season, although really it’s just his second as he missed his entire rookie season. He’s still raw, but expectations have been placed on him as he was thrown in as the starting left tackle last year when Tyler Guyton got hurt. He was also brought up in the discussion of a position battle with Guyton for the starting spot this year, but we’re not exactly sure what that’s about. He’s been regularly tested by the Cowboys first-team pass rushers, and that hasn’t gone very well as he’s struggled with guys blowing past him around the edge. Preseason game grade: C+ Starting at left tackle, he held his ground okay. He didn’t look spectacular, but he wasn’t horrid either. His length and wide base provided a strong wall for him, and his spring out of his stance looked good. Outside of a few moments where his balance was off, he did a fine job holding his blocks. He moved well in space, and he was never overpowered. He was a little antsy out of his stance, leaving early a couple times, although he only got caught once. As backups go, bigger expectations are put on him, but he played just fine. Roster security: Relatively safe as he still sits as the team’s top swing tackle option Nick Leverett The veteran has played in the league for five years on four different teams, but has less than a dozen starts under his belt. He signed with the Cowboys late last year and then a reserve/future deal early this year. He has been okay in camp, showing some good consistency in practice Preseason game grade: C+ He replaced Bass at center midway through the offense’s second drive. His performance was a lot like what he’s shown in practice. Nothing fancy, but sound. He got low and held his ground well. His leverage was firm as he displayed a solid anchor once engaged. The only issue he showed was his lateral agility. While he moves well for a guy with his bottom-heavy frame, his feet weren’t so quick to get into position, and oftentimes defenders can be seen flying by him. Roster security: In the hunt. It could come down to him and Cornelius for the final interior spot and his center flexibility could give him the nod. Trevor Keegan A fifth-round pick of the Eagles a couple of years ago, he was a star at Michigan, but was the odd man out as injuries and stacked talent made him expendable in Philly. The Cowboys pounced on the opportunity to add him to their group, and so far, things look good. His consistency has been an issue, as sometimes he’s looked absolutely dominant in training camp, while other times he’s shown that he still has some technical things to clean up. Preseason game grade: C Starting at left guard against Seattle, Keegan held up okay for the most part. When he got his hands on the defender, he secured the block, and he did a good job twisting his man to help seal off running lanes. He played a little upright, and his footwork was a bit clumpy. Many times in the game, you saw him losing balance and leaning a bit as the player got away from him. He showed good power, but just needed to get a little lower and sustain his blocks longer. Roster security: Stable. Making a strong push to be one of the team’s interior backups. Ajani Cornellis A late-round draft pick from a year ago, Cornelius was stashed as a development project with bigger expectations heading into year two. Sadly, those hopes have not come to fruition. The coaches have moved him inside to guard, hoping a new position will bring out his strengths and mask his deficiencies. Preseason game grade: C- Against the Seahawks, he started at right guard and put together a highly encouraging performance. He didn’t dominate, and there were some balance issues at times where defenders just side-stepped him out of the way, but then there were others where he used his athleticism to get into space to pull around on blocks. He moved well and locked up defenders, opening up holes for the running backs. It was a little erratic and uncontrolled at times, but he was pesky, and he was quick to look for the next guy to hit. He got to his spots and kept defenders at bay. Solid. Roster security: On the bubble. New life inside has opened up another path to make the team. Drew Shelton The rookie is this year’s top offensive investment, selected in the fourth round. His raw ability offers some nice upside, with the question being, how long before he’s ready to step in and be a consistent player? In camp, it’s been a little messy as the coaches have challenged him on either side, and he’s showing that he has a ways to go. Preseason game grade: D The struggles he’s shown in camp were on display against Seattle. The Seahawks backup edge rushers got around him with ease. He often was late figuring out which guy was coming, leaving him out of position. He failed to square up, often lunging or just going along for the ride. He was late getting his hands up and just looked lost. It felt like he was in recovery mode all game. Roster security: His draft investment should protect him for at least one season, but his performance up to this point makes him a fringe player who isn’t ready for primetime action. Marcellus Johnson A young but well-traveled UDFA, Johnson was signed by the Cowboys to provide some competition at the swing tackle position. He’s had issues with his footwork in camp and Preseason game grade: D- It was a rough outing for the team’s third-string tackle, where his balance and hand placement were all over the place. His most incriminating moment came when he was flagged for back-to-back penalties, first a false start, then an illegal hands-to-face. His feet were jittery and he never really got himself into a position to hold blocks. He kept throwing his hands upward near the neck area, never getting any good pushback, and then ultimately making contact with an opponent’s facemask. It was a sloppy performance and makes the team’s depth at tackle a little murky with both he and Shelton struggling. Roster security: In trouble. He needed a good showing to put himself in the conversation, and he’s not off to a good start.
author: Dan Rogers

title: 5 players on roster bubble after addition of Von Miller
summary: The Dallas Cowboys made a move for a veteran pass rusher Sunday night. The NFL’s ninth all-time leader in sacks, Von Miller, is signing with the team after spending most of the offseason waiting for the right opportunity. The newest Cowboy brings added veteran leadership to a pass rush unit that includes Rashan Gary, Donovan […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - OCTOBER 19: Von Miller #24 of the Washington Commanders rushes the passer during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Field on October 19, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys made a move for a veteran pass rusher Sunday night . The NFL’s ninth all-time leader in sacks, Von Miller, is signing with the team after spending most of the offseason waiting for the right opportunity. The newest Cowboy brings added veteran leadership to a pass rush unit that includes Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaki, and Malachi Lawrence. Outside of those three, adding Miller to the mix could create some uncertainty for other players looking to make the final 53-man roster. Here are four players who could be in danger now that Miller is in Dallas. Marist Liufau Former Cowboys third-round pick Marist Liufau took snaps at outside linebacker for the first time against the Seattle Seahawks on Saturday. The position change came this offseason as the team transitioned to a new defense under Christian Parker. Brian Schottenheimer has said the position change would be good for Liufau’s development. With the addition of Miller, the Liufau experiment could be running its course before it even started. There were highlight moments for the OLB on Saturday night, but there were multiple times he looked outmatched going against blockers at the line of scrimmage. Sam Williams The Cowboys brought back Sam Williams on a one-year prove-it deal after a very up-and-down tenure on his rookie contract. Williams had a great start to his career with 8.5 sacks over his first two years as a rotational player at defensive end, but injury derailed his third year, and he hasn’t looked like the same player since. The other thing that comes with Williams is penalties. There have been points throughout his career when a penalty comes up at the wrong time for a silly mistake. Add that to his mistakes off the field, and if the Cowboys are looking to change the culture in Dallas and give the room a makeover, Williams’ time in Dallas might come to an end with the addition of Miller. James Houston It’s James Houston! The Cowboys must have been happy to see the pass rusher have a few sacks in the game Saturday night (even if one was nullified by an accepted penalty). That should bode well for his chances to make the roster, but if Miller’s addition is considered an upgrade over Houston, Dallas might be willing to move on. Houston actually has the most appeal from a trade standpoint. If the Cowboys want to upgrade at offensive line with their depth, they might be able to hang Houston out there as trade bait to get something in return. Another area they could look to add would be cornerback. Dallas has a history of making trades right before the cut-down deadline. Houston could net something for the Cowboys after having a 5.5-sack season. Isaiah Land/Tyrus Wheat The final roster spots are usually reserved for players the team doesn’t want to cut, for fear they won’t come back to the practice squad. Isaiah Land and Tyrus Wheat are tied together in more ways than one. Both players were previously with the Cowboys as undrafted free agents and are now back in their second tenure with the team. They are also likely fighting each other for what could be the 53rd spot on the team. Wheat has been with Dallas the longest, making the team in 2023 and 2024 as a special teams player. Coming off a 1.5-sack season with the Detroit Lions, Wheat has flashed a lot more production as a pass rusher as of late. Land is more of a projection; his college stats made him an intriguing player to take a chance on, and he had a sack against the Seahawks on a critical fourth-down play. With Miller in the fold, Dallas might not have the luxury to develop one or both of them. There’s always a chance they come back on the practice squad, but cut defensive linemen are usually the first ones to be claimed on the waiver wire since it’s a premium position.

(Photo by Hyoung Chang/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Day 13 of Broncos Camp is complete, and it was the most intense, emotional, and physical practice yet. The pads were back on, and we saw multiple skirmishes and fights, including quarterback Bo Nix getting into it with star pass rusher Nik Bonitto. It was pretty spicy. Stacking the work days. 😤 pic.twitter.com/Omq4uKBN26 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 18, 2026 In today’s camp report, we have more about today’s chippy and intense practice and how quarterback Bo Nix loves it. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph gives some praise to rookie linebacker Red Murdock; offensive coordinator Davis Webb talks running back rotation and Jonah Coleman, injury updates, news and notes, tweets from camp, quotes, and more! Chippy and intense practice Today’s Broncos practice was one of the more intense and physical practices they have had in quite a while. It’s Day 13 of camp; they have been practicing against each other for over 2 weeks, and today, tempers flared in a big way. It all started early in practice when rookie tight end Justin Joly said something that pissed off the defense, and it quickly became a 4-on-1 defense vs. Joly skirmish. That was broken up, and practice continued. However, moments later, undrafted rookie linebacker Taurean York de-cleated Joly, who was on a crossing route, and the defense went wild. That happens at times throughout camp, and we move on. Things got spicier late when Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper collapsed the pocket on quarterback Bo Nix, and for the second time this practice, Nix went down. Thankfully, he was alright, but the Broncos’ starting quarterback was PISSED. Tempers would flare soon after when linebacker Alex Singleton got an INT off Nix, the ball got punched out, and all hell broke loose. We had a pile-up of players; Bonitto was heated, and Nix, still pissed about being knocked down and probably about the INT, pulled star edge rusher Nik Bonitto off the pile by his leg. Nix was pissed, Bonitto was pissed, and reserve center Calvin Throckmorton emerged from the pile bleeding from his face and would head to the locker room with a trainer holding an ice pack above his eye. Bo Nix on the fight at Broncos Training Camp: pic.twitter.com/2G4P82NkL7 — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) August 18, 2026 After practice, both Vance Joseph and Davis Webb told reporters that no matter what, you cannot hit the quarterback, which is a well known fact during training camp. Your season depends on Nix, and you don’t want to get him hurt from friendly fire. “Thought it was good. Obviously, you want competitive periods. It’s been competitive all camp. You know, offense wins, defense wins. You know, guys are getting guys better. Obviously, you can’t cross the line. That’s against the rules. So, you know, practice games. When we’re playing our style of football, you know, it’s aggressive. It’s downhill, but we can’t ever cross the line and hurt our play aggressively when when the quarterback is hit or hits the ground in camp. Do you talk to your guys about Listen, we Coach Payton talks about show to practice from day one and you know, we all know on defense to avoid the quarterback, right? It it gets competitive obviously and guys are rushing to win the down and sometimes they get too close, you know, and we simply remind them, but you know, Bo’s our quarterback and we don’t want anyone near Bo” Nix spoke to the media after practice and was asked about the events that went down during today’s practice, and he told reporters “I love it”. “I love it. It’s football. It’s getting me ready for the games coming up, and it’s a physical practice out there played by physical people. It got intense, and we were just really enjoying it and sometimes in the dog days of summer practice gets long and the intensity runs high. “ At the end of the day, Nix shouldn’t be getting touched or going down. It has happened twice this camp, so that’s non-negoitable for me. The rest of it? I love it. Nix has that dog in him and I want to see these two units have that fire in them. Obviously, nobody can get hurt and hopefully Throckmorton merely had a flesh wound, but overall, I like it. Get it out of your system and don’t let it carry over into Wednesday’s practice. These guys are ready to hit another team. Rookie LB Red Murdock has the mind and intelligence to call the Broncos’ defense One of the big winners from the preseason opener was rookie linebacker Red Murdock. He led the team in tackles and showed some promise. The final pick in the draft is far from being irrelevant and earned some big praise from defensive coordinator Vance Joseph after today’s practice. Red Murdock has the mind and intelligence to call the Broncos’ defense, per Vance Joseph pic.twitter.com/XKpuasaM21 — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 18, 2026 Joseph told reporters that Murdock did a good job of calling the defense this past week and that he has the mind and intelligence to call the Broncos defense “His college tape. It’s the draft [evaluation]. He was a smart football player that punched the ball out a lot, and we’ve seen it in practice. To be a Mike [line]backer in this league, it’s more than your physical traits; it’s your mind. That part he has. Now we have to use his mind to make more plays.” We heard how difficult it is to learn the Broncos defense last season from veteran Dre Greenlaw, so it is impressive that Murdock has this ability. Now, he may not know it fully yet, but this is good progress for the rookie who is looking more and more like a roster lock as we progress through the summer and training camp. Injury Report OL Nick Gargiulo remained on the PUP and did not practice today TE Caleb Lohner continued to miss practice LB Levelle Bailey suffered a broken leg vs. the Falcons and obviously did not practice today Edge rusher Drew Sanders did not practice again today and now has missed two straight practices WR Michael Bandy continued to sit out practice Backup center Alex Forsyth did not practice today Star WR Jaylen Waddle was in full pads today and practiced fully WR/KR Marvin Mims was in full pads today but was seen on the side field during team drills Veteran RB JK Dobbins was in full pads today Starting center Luke Wattenberg was in full pads today but was on the side field for team drills Backup offensive lineman Calvin Throckmorton, who has recently been the starting center, left practice after a skirmish involving multiple teammates. He was seen bleeding on his face and holding an ice pack above his eye News and Notes Broncos were back in pads today for the first of two padded training camp practices before their Week 2 preseason game vs. the Green Bay Packers Broncos defense dominated the final move-the-ball periods – PBUs by PS2, Brandon Jones, and Ja’Quan McMillian LB Alex Singleton had an INT on QB Bo Nix WR Courtland Sutton had a deep completion against CB Riley Moss, where he went up and “Moss’d” the Broncos’ starting corner QB Jarrett Stidham had a completion to….Frank Crum? Possible ‘Joker’ in the making QB Bo Nix had a TD pass to WR Troy Franklin, but he’s lucky it wasn’t an INT due to going right through the hands of CB Ja’Quan McMillian UDFA LB Taurean York de-cleated rookie TE Justin Joly WR Troy Franklin made a diving catch on a throw from QB Sam Ehlinger – Sounds like it was a good day for him UDFA WR Cam Ross was getting targets from QB Bo Nix during team drills, but dropped the ball – He appears to be someone to watch moving forward Nix had a 30-yard completion down the sideline to WR Jaylen Waddle Rookie DT Tyler Onyedim came in for Zach Allen on a play and had a pressure and a possible sack Tweets from Camp Jaylen Waddle ready for Day 13 🔥 (Also seen: Coop feelin’ himself 😅) #KOABroncosCamp pic.twitter.com/oN5oqNE5UM — KOA…

title: Inside linebackers stepping up to the challenge for Broncos
summary: For established players in the NFL, the preseason isn’t arduous. It’s the calm before the storm. But for rookies and undrafted free agents, it’s the exact opposite. It is the storm. One big play could be the difference between making the team or finding yourself on the outside looking in. The latter rings true for […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, CO - AUGUST 1: Red Murdock #50 of the Denver Broncos participates in training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on August 1, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images For established players in the NFL, the preseason isn’t arduous. It’s the calm before the storm. But for rookies and undrafted free agents, it’s the exact opposite. It is the storm. One big play could be the difference between making the team or finding yourself on the outside looking in. The latter rings true for several inside linebackers for the Denver Broncos that are vying for a spot on this year’s final 53-man roster. Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad will be Denver’s top duo at the position in 2026. That’s etched in stone. However, the battle for who earns the backup spots behind them continue to intensify. Unfortunately, the team’s depth at the position took a hit in preseason opener against the Atlanta Falcons with Levelle Bailey suffering a broken leg . With Jordan Turner absent from the game after recently being activated from the NFI list , three players saw significant snaps against the Falcons: Red Murdock, Taurean York, and Karene Reid. For Murdock and York, it was their first in-game reps in the pros. With respect to Reid, a chance to show he deserves a spot after playing in ten games with the team as a UDFA last season. After yesterday’s practice, Head Coach Sean Payton noted he was pleased with what he saw from the trio of linebackers in Atlanta. “They got good snaps, valuable snaps. It was good exposure for them, part of the process. We did a lot of things we wanted to accomplish, so it was good to see those guys get the work,” stated Payton. Red Murdock had a very promising debut for the #Broncos . Play strength to fight through screens and exceptional open-field tackling ability highlight his preseason opener. pic.twitter.com/ahMWDvuKyQ — Andy (@AndyyNFL) August 17, 2026 It’s a complex position to learn. However, Payton noted that all of them have picked things up quickly and is encouraged with their progress. “You have the run fits, you have the pass game, you have the calls. If you’re calling the defense, you’ve kind of got quite a bit and you’re hoping that comes instinctually. They’re not going to pick it up right away, but they learn quickly,” added Payton. The last pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Mr. Irrelevant , Murdock was anything but in his NFL debut. A bright spot throughout training camp, Murdock has impressed teammates and coaches with his intelligence and nose for the football. The two-time first-team All-MAC standout logged the most snaps of any defensive player against the Falcons with 47. He also led the team in tackles with eight. Next in line for snap share was second-year linebacker Reid. He had four tackles on 28 snaps—as well as the key tip which resulted in cornerback Jahdae Barron’s 97-yard pick six. York, the UDFA rookie linebacker from Texas A&M, finished the game with two tackles on 22 snaps. With just two preseason games remaining and a little less than two weeks before roster cutdowns, every opportunity and rep will matter for Denver’s young group of inside linebackers. In reality, it’s not just for a spot on the roster. It’s about proving they can be the ‘next man up’ if need be. Who will that be? That’s yet to be determined, but based on what we saw versus the Falcons, I’d say Murdock has the inside track for the LB3 position.

title: Broncos roster 2026: Ja’Quan McMillian, Dasan McCullough, Red Murdock are underrated
summary: In the Houston Texans Hidden Gems piece, I posited that the Texans were the NFL’s great “what-if” team of the 2025 season, because if their offense had been even league-average in the playoffs, that defense could have taken them all the way to the Super Bowl. Well, if the Texans weren’t last year’s great “what-if” […]
full_text: In the Houston Texans Hidden Gems piece , I posited that the Texans were the NFL’s great “what-if” team of the 2025 season, because if their offense had been even league-average in the playoffs, that defense could have taken them all the way to the Super Bowl. Well, if the Texans weren’t last year’s great “what-if” team, the Denver Broncos certainly were. What if Bo Nix hadn’t suffered a broken ankle near the end of Denver’s 33-30 overtime divisional round win over the Buffalo Bills? It’s pretty likely that Nix would have engineered more than the seven points the Broncos scored in their 10-7 AFC Championship loss to the New England Patriots with backup Jarrett Stidham, and who knows what a Super Bowl XLVIII rematch between the Broncos and the Seattle Seahawks would have looked like? In any regard, the 2026 Broncos showed that they were not messing around when it came to the future when they sent 2026 first-, third-, and fourth-round picks to the Miami Dolphins for receiver Jaylen Waddle and a 2026 fourth-round pick. Vertical juice was missing in Sean Payton’s passing game last season, and that’s something Waddle can provide in spades. Woo, buddy. Jaylen Waddle adds SO much to Sean Payton's passing game. Toughness over the middle, vertical juice, route awareness, and the understanding of how to kill zone coverage. Bo Nix must be crying happy tears right now. And Waddle gets a major QB arm improvement. pic.twitter.com/hnxny8GbCz — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) March 17, 2026 Adding Waddle to an offense that ranked 15th in DVOA last season, and bringing back the entire defense that ranked fifth, would seem to put a healthy Broncos team in the same catbird seat they seemed to occupy last season before losing their franchise quarterback. Of course, we can never be sure of these things. All sorts of stuff can happen during an NFL season, and if these Broncos want to win their first championship since the end of the 2015 season, it’ll take the best from everybody on the roster — not just the justified stars, but also the guys whose name recognition has lagged behind their on-field accomplishments. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems on the Broncos’ 2026 roster — one underrated veteran, one underrated free agent, and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: DB Ja’Quan McMillian If you want to go deep into the playoffs, you need players who recognize the biggest moments, and step up accordingly. Per the team’s official website , defensive back Ja’Quan McMillian has no problem with this concept. Last season, the 2022 undrafted free agent from East Carolina… …recorded a game-clinching strip-sack in Denver’s opening win of the season over Tennessee, notched an interception and key third-down sack in a win over the Chiefs and had a pick six in a victory over the Chargers. McMillian also picked off Josh Allen in overtime of the Broncos’ Divisional Round win to help set up Denver’s game-winning drive. Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss are the Broncos’ established outside cornerbacks, but Vance Joseph’s defense doesn’t work as well without McMillian doing everything he does. And we do mean everything he does. Last season, the 5’10”, 183-pound McMillian allowed 55 catches on 81 targets for 502 yards, 243 yards after the catch, two touchdowns, three interceptions, six pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 77.3. McMillian also had 47 solo tackles, 27 stops, six tackles for loss, two forced fumbles, four sacks, and eight total pressures, because the dude is a guided missile who is constantly looking to create chaos. Whether he's messing with protections at the line of scrimmage or denying receivers their catches in the open field, Ja'Quan McMillian of the @Broncos is one of the more effectively chaotic DBs in the NFL today. pic.twitter.com/v7M16pBMyT — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 17, 2026 “His mindset is off the charts,” Surtain said of McMillian over the summer. “The way that he carries himself on and off the field and his work ethic… There are only a few that quite work like him. Being undrafted and coming in, nobody knew about him. Now, he’s a hot commodity. It goes to show the work that he’s put in, and how much he values and hones in on his craft. I’m excited for J-Mac. He’s a big-time player, and I’m happy that he is finally getting his spotlight.” Now, with a new second-round Restricted Free Agent tender contract under his belt, McMillian should continue his status as one of the best nickel defenders in the NFL — and still one of the most underrated. Underrated free agent: EDGE Dasan McCullough The Broncos didn’t do much in free agency, because you don’t need to when you’re returning 21 of 22 estimated starters from the 2025 season, and Jaylen Waddle is the new guy. So, I looked through the team’s undrafted free agents instead, and one name made me do the eyebrow thing — Nebraska EDGE Dasan McCullough. And that was before the backstory came into focus. McCullough’s father Deland was a running back at Miami (Ohio) in 1994, and his first-time playcaller was an offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach by the name of… Sean Payton . A cool #Broncos UDFA connection: Nebraska OLB Dasan McCullough's dad, Deland, is Oklahoma's RB coach. In 1994 Deland was an RB at Miami (Ohio). He had a first-time playcaller: Sean Payton. Payton later had Deland in for a workout with the Eagles, which Deland recalled this way: pic.twitter.com/CBzlelrukh — Parker Gabriel (@ParkerJGabriel) April 26, 2026 Injuries got in the way of Deland’s NFL dreams, but now, there’s the opportunity for Dasan to get it all done for the family. Certainly, the Broncos considered selecting McCullough late in the 2026 draft. Ultimately, he signed a $245,000 UDFA contract with a $20,000 signing bonus, one of the biggest such deals the Broncos have ever given anybody. Last season for the Cornhuskers, the younger McCullough had two sacks and 16 pressures in just 155 pass-rushing snaps. The 6’5:, 235-pound McCullough fits the Vance Joseph ideal of leaner edge guys who just singe tackles and tight ends with their speed around the edge off the snap. The athletic potential is there, and you can see the embryonic version of a Nik Bonitto type at certain times. Dasan McCullough seems like an ideal Vance Joseph EDGE in that he looks like he's been shot out of a cannon most of the time. If he can get his technique together and tweak his GPS in space, there might be something here. @Broncos pic.twitter.com/ZUstsgnDzZ — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 15, 2026 “They’re already a really good team with a bunch of really good pass-rushers, and I feel like my skill set definitely fits in that room perfectly with how they play,’’ Dasan said after he signed that contract. “And with Vance Joseph being there and developing his system, I definitely see my career skyrocketing under him… I’m really physical. I’m just really a fast, relentless guy. You always see me running to the ball hard.” Obviously, Payton isn’t going to give a roster spot to a rookie based on family ties, but with a strong preseason, who knows what Dasan McCullough is capable of down the road? Underrated draft pick: LB Red Murdock I almost went with fourth-round running back Jonah Coleman here, because I believe that Coleman is seriously underrated as a big-play threat . But when Buffalo linebacker Red Murdock was Mr. Irrelevant in the 2026 draft — the last player selected with the 257th overall pick — he was my guy. Because there was no way the 6’2”, 232-pound Murdock should have gone that low. In 2025, his fourth season at Buffalo, Murdock had 93 solo tackles, 56 stops, seven tackles for loss, six forced fumbles. He also had six sacks and 20 pressures… on just 47 pass-rushing snaps. Not a bad return rate there. “Murdock, just man… he’s a tackling machine,” GM George Paton said of that pick after it was made. “Just really instinctive. Really good against the run. He may hold the record — you guys may know — for…

title: Horse Tracks: Broncos’ defense picks up where it left off
summary: Sean Payton acknowledged there are “just a handful of things” he might be mad about following the 27-7 preseason win over the Falcons last weekend, but that would be an improvement over his mood following the first preseason game last year when he had “14 things to be pissed off about.” And other than “too […]
full_text: Sean Payton acknowledged there are “just a handful of things” he might be mad about following the 27-7 preseason win over the Falcons last weekend, but that would be an improvement over his mood following the first preseason game last year when he had “ 14 things to be pissed off about .” And other than “too many penalties,” Payton admitted there was a lot to like in the Falcons game, calling it a “good first time out.” After watching the tape over the weekend, the head coach was still pleased with the players’ performance. “It was good in a lot of areas. I thought the intent, the focus was good overall,” he added. “There’s enough on there to coach off of where there are some techniques we can clean up, but I thought overall for the first time out it was good.” WHAT A CATCH BY COURTLAND SUTTON "We've gotta start talking about this Denver Broncos team a lot more" ~ @DariusJButler #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/tEirt3qY6b — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 17, 2026 Among the “good” was a defense that not only looked like it picked up where it left off last season, but that it had improved. With one sack, nine QB pressures and three tackles for a loss, the pass rush was decent all night — as expected. But two takeaways from different defenders perhaps signaled an area of improvement after being an area of emphasis this offseason. “Got our hands on a couple. …We had a chance for two or three more. We got the sleeves on. I think there’s some things we can be better at; that was encouraging,” Payton said after the game. “I like the energy we played with.” Replacing John Franklin-Myers was one of the Broncos' biggest unanswered questions entering the preseason. After one game, Denver's plan on the defensive line is coming into focus. | via @ErickTrickel https://t.co/XEWZhT070O — Mile High Huddle (@MileHighHuddle) August 17, 2026 Defensive tackle Zach Allen definitely liked it. “Yes, it’s definitely encouraging. We played a really good football team, and they played their starters for the most part,” Allen said. “When [a takeaway] happens, it’s exciting and obviously we have to just keep working it every day and hopefully it translates into the regular season.” While there had been concern about replacing John Franklin Myers on the line, several young guys last week showed they were ready to step up. “That’s just a character thing,” Allen added. “The good thing is we have a bunch of guys that think like that on this team. Any time you roll the ball out, you want to win. Culture is a huge thing, especially in this league. We just want to keep on doing it.” With most guys returning and a lot of young talent for Vance Joseph to coach up, preseason isn’t just a time for this defense to get on the same page, it’s a chance to build on previous success. “I think definitely out here there’s probably more experimentation,” Allen added. “We definitely want to keep a couple of things under our hat for the regular season, but if the basics are working in the preseason games, especially if you’re going against starters, it’s huge. … There’s still a lot more work to do and [we] just have to take it day by day.” I’ve been saying it all camp long: Broncos will have the No. 1 defense in the NFL this season. Takeaways will help put them over the edge. Plus the hole left by JFM doesn’t seem to loom as large as we thought. Roach, Uwazurike & co. seem rather formidable in his place. https://t.co/03qaQZWgv8 — AROD – Anthony Rodriguez (@AnthonyRod33) August 17, 2026

title: Former Lions CB Terrion Arnold won’t be able to play for Seahawks right away
summary: Former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold appears to be headed for the Seattle Seahawks, but there are a few roadblocks in the way before the former first-round pick can see the field. Arnold and the Seahawks have agreed upon a contract, but Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said recently that they’re working through some things […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 22: Terrion Arnold #6 of the Detroit Lions looks on during an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on September 22, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold appears to be headed for the Seattle Seahawks, but there are a few roadblocks in the way before the former first-round pick can see the field. Arnold and the Seahawks have agreed upon a contract, but Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said recently that they’re working through some things before they officially sign him . “We’re working through that and when’s the best time for him to come in, but we have an agreement with him and we’ll see,” Macdonald said.“But I just really don’t know what, you know, how we’re gonna do it.” Arnold is currently facing eight felony charges from an incident in Florida involving an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping. According to the latest reports, his next court date in the trial is Oct. 5. According to the latest report from Ian Rapoport, this process is expected to move slowly for the Seahawks, and “it will take a while” before they sign Arnold. One huge blockade in this process is the fact that Arnold, according to Rapoport, will go on the Commissioner Exempt List once he signs with a team. What is the Commissioner Exempt List? Basically, it’s a designation that can only be made by NFL commissioner Roger Goodell for players in “unusual circumstances.” Players on the exempt list are allowed to attend meetings, go through workouts, and receive treatment from the team. However, they are not allowed to play or practice during that time. How long a player stays on the list is completely up to the commissioner. So in the case with Arnold, it could be until his legal proceedings are complete. It could be longer than that. It could be shorter than that. Despite all of that, Rapoport says the Seahawks still intend to sign Arnold. It’s just not clear when—and if —he’ll be able to play for Seattle this season.

title: Lions rookie LB Jimmy Rolder provides very optimistic injury update
summary: At the start of training camp, the Detroit Lions got some bad luck. Fourth-round pick Jimmy Rolder suffered a hamstring injury that coach Dan Campbell described as something that will keep him out “a while,” but wasn’t a season ender. Another report suggested it wasn’t a severe injury, but that he’ll still “miss some time.” […]
full_text: Detroit Lions linebacker Jimmy Rolder (41) during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 29, 2026. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images At the start of training camp, the Detroit Lions got some bad luck. Fourth-round pick Jimmy Rolder suffered a hamstring injury that coach Dan Campbell described as something that will keep him out “a while,” but wasn’t a season ender. Another report suggested it wasn’t a severe injury, but that he’ll still “miss some time.” Well, this week we got some news right from the source, and it’s a lot more optimistic than those two updates. On an appearance on “Xs and Bros” podcast with Matt Shepard, Rolder himself gave an update that could drastically change how the Lions’ linebacker room shapes out . “Leg is getting better. We’re definitely making some strides. I’ll be back out there in a week—week or so. We’ll see,” Rolder said. Now, Rolder isn’t exactly clear on whether being “out there” means regularly working with a trainer or truly returning to practice, but it’s still a significant and positive development for the rookie linebacker. If Rolder returns to practice before the end of training camp, he’ll almost assuredly avoid being placed on injured reserve, where he’d be forced to miss the first four games of the season. That would drastically change the look of the linebacker room, which currently includes a competitive group of veterans fighting for a spot. While Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Devin White feel like locks, if Rolder makes the 53-man roster without going to IR, he could threaten the spots for Damone Clark and Trevor Nowaske, among others. We’ll see just how quickly Rolder returns to the field and if he’ll avoid the IR soon, as roster cuts are due less than two weeks away on Aug. 30.

title: Observations from Detroit Lions training camp full scrimmage
summary: On Day 14 of 2026 training camp, the Detroit Lions held their annual “night practice,” where they ran a full-squad scrimmage. The team splits in half, with the first-team offense pairing with the second- and third-team defense, while the defensive starters pair with the offensive reserves. It’s a fun, fast-paced practice with a lot of […]
full_text: Aug 2, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. looks on during Detroit Lions training camp at Meijer Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On Day 14 of 2026 training camp, the Detroit Lions held their annual “night practice,” where they ran a full-squad scrimmage. The team splits in half, with the first-team offense pairing with the second- and third-team defense, while the defensive starters pair with the offensive reserves. It’s a fun, fast-paced practice with a lot of information to absorb, but fortunately, because this happened to fall on the same day we held our Pride of Detroit podcast from Allen Park, I had some help: Jeremy Reisman, Ryan Mathews, Meko Scott, and Al Karsten were all in attendance. The Lions were careful to limit practice time for several players in this scrimmage, not wanting to re-aggravate anyone dealing with a soft tissue injury from the past week. As a result, current starting center Juice Scruggs only played in the first half and was replaced by Seth McLaughlin. We already have a full injury recap on the website with more detail , including good news about Jameson Williams’ “little shoulder” injury. In total, over four nine-minute quarters, the Lions ran 15 drives, mainly matching starters vs. starters (1 vs. 1) and reserves vs. reserves (2 vs. 2), and we’ll provide highlights from each drive in our observations: Drive 1: 1 vs. 1 — Rough start for the offense The Lions offense got off to a very slow start, opening practice with a botched snap exchange (Scruggs at center). On the second play, pressure from Alim McNeill forced a tougher throw, and D.J. Reed was tight in coverage, forcing a pass breakup. Facing third and long, Jared Goff connected with Sam LaPorta, but it fell short of the sticks, and the offense was forced to punt (simulated). Drive 2: 2 vs. 2 — Ennis Rakestraw shines On the first play for the reserves, they elected to kick things off with a run, but Ennis Rakestraw crashed from his corner position and made a quick stop after just two yards. Another run on second down saw Rakestraw crash again, this time getting into the backfield for a tackle for a two-yard loss. On third down, facing third-and-10, quarterback Luke Altmyer got caught on his heels a bit after a Christian Izien blitz (there was a lot of blitzing from defensive backs in this scrimmage) and sailed a pass over Tay Martin. Another three-and-out and simulated punt. Drive 3: 1 vs. 1 — McNeill is a problem Rookie nickel Keith Abney blitzed to kick off the third drive, but Jahmyr Gibbs did a nice job picking it up and allowing Goff to hit Brock Wright on a crosser, gaining around four yards. Gibbs was rewarded with a carry on the next snap, but pressure from McNeill and Levi Onwuzurike limited the back to just a yard. Goff misses Amon-Ra St.Brown on third down, and the offense is quickly off the field again. Drive 4: 2 vs. 2 — Rakestraw interception Altmyer opened drive four with another overthrow after another blitz from a defensive back, this time from Rakestraw, who may have tipped the ball and altered its trajectory. The offense goes back to the ground on second down, but Onwuzurike showed off his power and shed McLaughlin and made the stop in the hole for no gain. Facing another third-and-long, Altmyer forced a pass over the middle, but Rakestraw (and Izien) were able to jump the pass and came away with an interception. Drive 5: 1 vs. 1 — Fourth down stop The starters open this drive with a Gibbs run, but backside pursuit from McNeill and frontside pressure from Tyleik Williams eliminated running lanes, with Williams getting the stop at the line. The offense swapped Gibbs for Vaki and tried to catch the defense off guard with another run, but it was also stopped in its tracks. On third down, pressure up the middle from Skyler Gill-Howard may have resulted in another sack, but coaches let the play go on, with Goff connecting with St. Brown for a moderate gain. On fourth down (and three yards), the offense stayed on the field; Goff targeted LaPorta, but safety Thomas Harper was tight in coverage and forced an incompletion, possibly getting credit for a PBU. Drive 6: 2 vs. 2 — Chuck Clark interception The reserves opened the drive with a Jacob Saylors run to the right, following a duo block from Mason Miller and Colby Sorsdal, where Sorsdal climbed to the linebacker, leading to a seven-yard gain for Saylors. They run it again on second down, but Izien set a firm edge, forcing the run back inside for a minimal gain. On third and short, the Lions ran again, this time with Jabari Small, who ran into a brick wall of defenders, but coaches said he got enough to move the chains—the first time this had happened so far in practice. With a fresh set of downs, Altmyer dropped back to throw, but pressure from Trevor Nowaske resulted in a sack and loss of six yards. Altmyer got a lot of those yards back on a quick slant to Malik Cunningham, taking advantage of off-coverage and gaining 12 yards. Looking to convert another first down, Altmyer targets Dominic Lovett, but overshot him, and Chuck Clark was in waiting for an easy interception. Drive 7: 1 vs. 1 — Tom Kennedy touchdown After a dismal start, the offense finally strung some plays together to sustain a drive. A short Gibbs run resulted in just two yards, followed by an incompletion (targeting St. Brown with Jack Campbell in coverage), setting up third-and-long, but a cleverly executed run play resulted in a big gain. On the play, both Tate Ratledge and Blake Miller pulled, overloading the run path and carving out a large hole for Gibbs to sprint through, resulting in a 21-yard run for the first team offense—and their first first-down conversion of practice. Now in the red zone, a defensive penalty on first down gave the Lions offense a first-and-five to continue the drive, and Goff took advantage with a quick slant to St. Brown for another first down. Vaki bounced a run to the right, but a crashing Khalil Dorsey saved a touchdown and kept it to a four-yard gain. Another bad snap from Scruggs pushed the offense back a couple of yards, but they didn’t let that hinder them, and on third down, Goff hit Tom Kennedy on a quick slant (a bit of a pick play with St. Brown) for a touchdown. Starting offense (and reserve defense) is up 7-0. Drive 8: 2/3 vs. 2/3 — Ahmed Hassanein sacks The Lions went a little deeper into their bench for this drive, and Dobbs took over for Altmyer for his only drive of practice. Pressure from the edge forced Dobbs into a jump throw that Joe Bachie undercut and got his hands on the pass for the breakup. Inside pressure from Ahmed Hassanein (who lined up over the guard) forced Dobbs into a quick pass that gained around eight yards, with Raheem Blackshear converting the first down on a three-yard run on the next play. Blackshear ran the ball again on first down but was stopped after just a one-yard gain. Defensive tackle Chris Smith wrecked the offense on second down, overpowering Mason Miller for the sack and an eight-yard loss. A defensive penalty made it third-and-13, but Hassanein (now back on the edge) was joined by Anthony Lucas in the backfield, and either could have gotten credit for sacking Dobbs and ending the drive. Drive 9: 1 vs. 1 — Tyleik Williams clogs the middle Goff opened this drive with a 12-yard pass to St. Brown, who started to chirp at the defense as the offense’s confidence returned. On the next first down, Goff had to throw the next pass in the dirt after what looked like a “choice” route from Gibbs put them on opposite pages. A Gibbs run on the next play gained positive yards for the offense, but Williams stuffed the middle of the line and limited the damage to just two yards. A slant from St. Brown gained the offense another five yards, setting up fourth-and-three, and while the offense stayed on the field, they were only trying to get the defense to jump offside…

title: Breaking down the Detroit Lions’ 3 GRIT Plays of the Week vs. Bengals
summary: We’ve spent five years hearing Dan Campbell tell us about GRIT.  ESPN has had “C’mon Man!” and “Jacked Up!” on “Monday Night Countdown”, while NFL Network has given us “Angry Runs” on “Good Morning Football.“ And of course “You Got Mossed!” on “Sunday NFL Countdown.“ I figure it’s time we start punching some holes in […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 13: Josh Johnson #11 of the Cincinnati Bengals runs the ball against Skyler Gill-Howard #50 of the Detroit Lions during the second half of the preseason game at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve spent five years hearing Dan Campbell tell us about GRIT. ESPN has had “C’mon Man!” and “Jacked Up!” on “Monday Night Countdown”, while NFL Network has given us “Angry Runs” on “Good Morning Football.“ And of course “You Got Mossed!” on “Sunday NFL Countdown.“ I figure it’s time we start punching some holes in a GRIT card . “It’s our core foundation, men. Grit,” Dan Campbell told the Lions during the season opener of HBO’s “Hard Knocks” in 2022. It’s written on the walls all over Allen Park. So each week, I’m going to find a few plays that I think best demonstrate GRIT. Here are my three from preseason Week 1. Seth McLaughlin looking for work McLaughlin initially punches the 1-technique to his right while keeping his eyes to his left for any stunt or blitz rusher. Once right guard Miles Frazier squares up on the block, McLaughlin is free. No stunt or blitz player emerges in his assigned gap, so McLaughlin starts looking for work. That’s when he sees left guard Christian Mahogany engaged with the 3-technique and comes over with a nasty shot to the ribs to help clean up the block. Skyler Gill-Howard refuses to stop The former linebacker showed off his instincts, athleticism and passion for the game on this third-and-5 in the fourth quarter. Gill-Howard gets held as Josh Johnson escapes the pocket, but he doesn’t stop chasing the Bengals quarterback. His persistence and pursuit allows him to track Johnson down, holding Cincinnati to a field goal. Dan Campbell called it one of his favorite plays from the game . Some defensive tackles would stop after being held when the quarterback scrambles in the fourth quarter of a preseason game. Some defensive tackles are not Skyler Gill-Howard. Ahmed Hassanein doesn’t let the moment distract him Hassanein had a big night with two sacks, but that’s not what impressed me most. Following his first sack, Hassanein showed the emotion that came with his return to the field after last season’s injury. It was an authentic celebration after an impassioned journey back to the field. It would be easy for a young player to get caught up in that moment and not be as dialed in on the next play. But Hassanein, despite being raw and relatively new to football, relentlessly attacked the next play. The Bengals run a screen pass to his side. Hassanein adjusts from his vertical pass rush, takes a strong pursuit angle and gets in on the third-down stop. The sack was the highlight. The response on the next play is the GRIT. Vote for the GRIT Play of the Week Three plays. Three different versions of GRIT. Now it’s your turn.

title: How preseason game 1 shifted Detroit Lions’ roster bubble on defense
summary: In the Detroit Lions’ 16-14 preseason loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, the defense put on a bit of a show. Despite playing their backups against Joe Burrow and several Bengals starters on offense, the Lions managed to hold Cincinnati to just 10 points and a mere 125 yards in the first half. They were able […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive back Nick Whiteside (38) warms up before OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, June 11, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co In the Detroit Lions’ 16-14 preseason loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, the defense put on a bit of a show. Despite playing their backups against Joe Burrow and several Bengals starters on offense, the Lions managed to hold Cincinnati to just 10 points and a mere 125 yards in the first half. They were able to do so off the back of a ton of great individual performances Thursday night. So in our Week 4 installment of “Bubble Watch,” we examine how the preseason performance has shifted our predictions for who is in and who is out for the 2026 53-man roster. View Link Defensive end : Assumed in: Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, Derrick Moore Ahmed Hassanein: 11 “IN” votes (no change) Payton Turner: 0 votes (no change) Anthony Lucas: 0 votes There hasn’t been much movement at defensive end in a few weeks, as Hassanein inches closer to being a roster lock at this point. His two-sack performance against the Bengals only seems to have solidified his spot. The question at this point is if anyone on the roster can justify keeping a fifth defensive end. Payton Turner can’t make the field, and Anthony Lucas has shown flashes, but maybe Eric O’Neill has earned some recent consideration . Defensive tackle: Assumed in: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams Levi Onwuzurike: 11 votes (no change) Tyler Lacy: 11 votes (no change) Skyle Gill-Howard: 11 votes (up 1) Chris Smith: 10 votes (up 5) Mekhi Wingo: 0 votes (down 2) Tyre West: 0 votes (no change) Chris Smith takes the second-biggest jump of any Lions defender in this week’s Bubble Watch, and that’s likely due to coach Dan Campbell going off on a rant about how much he appreciates Smith . “He plays disciplined football. He’s a grinder, man. He’ll do it. He’ll take on double teams for 60 plays if you ask him to do it,” Campbell said. “And that’s a thankless job, and it’s hard, and it’s nobody really sees that. You don’t get any love. But he doesn’t care. To him, that means more to him to know that he’s keeping his linebacker free like that’s his heaven. So, it’s unselfish, and it’s hard. It’s a nasty job, and it’s not for everybody. And so that’s why you appreciate it.” Meanwhile, after making two huge impact plays in the preseason, rookie Skyler Gill-Howard is now a unanimous “IN” from our staff. I initially had Onwuzurike out because of a slow start to camp, but then Campbell offered some encouraging words on Sunday. “I like Levi. I feel like Levi’s had a good camp,” Campbell said. “Levi, as we all know, he’s coming off a ton of injuries. But it’s nice to have two ACLs, he would tell you that. It helps him move a lot better, he’s got a lot more power and I think that shows up.” Linebacker: Assumed in: Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez Devin White: 11 votes (no change) Trevor Nowaske: 10 votes (no change) Damone Clark: 8 votes (down 2) Troy Reeder: 1 votes (down 1) Jimmy Rolder: 0 votes (down 3) Erick Hunter: 0 votes (no change) Joe Bachie: 0 votes (no change) While we saw some encouraging signs of Jimmy Rolder’s recovery progressing when he was working with a trainer over the weekend, our entire staff believes he’ll start the season on injured reserve and miss the first four games of the season. Meanwhile, Damone Clark’s continued absence at training camp due to an injury is starting to force him further down the roster bubble. At this point, it looks like some of our staff is comfortable just keeping five linebackers and using that roster spot somewhere else. Cornerback: Assumed in: DJ Reed, Rock Ya-Sin, Keith Abney New to bubble watch: Ennis Rakestraw: 11 votes Nick Whiteside: 11 votes (no change) Roger McCreary: 11 votes (up 6) Khalil Dorsey: 9 votes (down 1) McCreary had been sliding down our roster bubble for weeks, but a very strong performance in the preseason opener against the Bengals has him shooting right back up to a unanimous “IN.” Those extra votes are likely coming from the safety positions where—spoiler—everyone now believes both Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph will start on the PUP. Then there’s Ennis Rakestraw, who we are no longer assuming is in. He’s struggled in training camp and his preseason opener was extremely tough. He ceded several catches and suffered a minor injury against the Bengals. Still, our entire staff believes he’s on the right side of the bubble, likely due to his potential. And he lived up to that promise with an awesome performance during Monday night’s training camp scrimmage (after our votes had been submitted). Personally, I think the lack of faith in Dorsey is misguided. He’s a key special teamer and even got a little work with the first-team defense in recent practices. But I can understand the hesitation to keep seven cornerbacks. Safety Assumed in: Christian Izien, Avonte Maddox, Chuck Clark Thomas Harper: 11 votes (no change) Dan Jackson: 1 vote (up 1) Brian Branch: 0 votes (down 3) Kerby Joseph: 0 votes (no change) As I mentioned above, we’ve all got Branch and Joseph starting the season on PUP now, which leaves this room relatively straightforward. If Dan Jackson can make some big special teams plays over the next two weeks, though, he could certainly make a case for a fifth safety.

title: Discussion: Who is the top sleeper pick to make the Detroit Lions’ roster?
summary: The Detroit Lions are well past the midway point of training camp. In fact, roster cutdown day is less than two weeks away, with teams needing to shrink their roster by Sunday, August 30. For a roster like the Detroit Lions’, the top 40 spots are likely already pretty set. This camp didn’t see many […]
full_text: Aug 2, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions defensive end Eric O'Neill (66) looks on during Detroit Lions training camp at Meijer Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions are well past the midway point of training camp. In fact, roster cutdown day is less than two weeks away, with teams needing to shrink their roster by Sunday, August 30. For a roster like the Detroit Lions’, the top 40 spots are likely already pretty set. This camp didn’t see many starting jobs up for grabs, and some of the reserve jobs were already pretty locked in, too. However, those niche roles as third stringers or primary special teamers have a ton of competition, and it’s only heating up as we get deeper into training camp. There are some obvious names fighting for those roles, but there are a few late-rising sleepers to consider, as well. So today’s Question of the Day is: Who is your sleeper pick to make the Lions roster? My answer: Based on all of the training camp practices I’ve seen, there are four players I would categorize as sleepers who have flashed over the past few weeks and could sneak their way onto the 53-man roster. WR Tay Martin The cat is out of the bag already with coach Dan Campbell offering high praise for Martin on several occasions. “Tay Martin showed up again,” Campbell said after the first preseason game. “Blocking, made a one-on-one catch separated, special teams. He forced a penalty and that was just one play on special teams. He made more than that.” And now with Martin getting some work with the first-team offense, it’s clear this coaching staff has valued the work he’s put in thus far. I still think he’s a sleeper pick, though, because he was literally No. 90 on our roster rankings last month . For that WR5 or WR6 role, you need to be a special teams standout, and that’s exactly what Martin has done. EDGE Eric O’Neill O’Neill has really come on as of recently, and it all culminated in a pick-six during Monday’s scrimmage. The undrafted rookie should still be considered a relative long-shot to make the roster given Detroit’s investments in the edge defender position this offseason, but I would not be surprised to see him land on the practice squad and even possibly get the call-up during the season. DT Ben Stille It feels like #62 has appeared in my notes daily over the last week. The Lions are Stille’s sixth NFL team since entering the league as an undrafted rookie in 2022. He’s only played in 18 games and started one, but he’s got some nice twitch to him, and he’s got a knack for getting to the quarterback in these training camp practices. The depth isn’t great at defensive tackle here in Detroit, so he does have a realistic path to the roster if the Lions sour on guys like Levi Onwuzurike, Mekhi Wingo, and/or Tyre West. LB Erick Hunter Hunter went undrafted out of Morgan State this year, and due to the jump in competition in the NFL, coach Campbell said Hunter still “doesn’t know what he doesn’t know.” But he’s a tenacious player, gives relentless effort, and has shown up several times making an impact on special teams. With the Lions’ linebacker room a little beat up right now (no Jimmy Rolder or Damone Clark), Hunter could sneak his way onto the roster. Which Lions player do you think is a sleeper pick to make the roster? Share your thoughts in the comment section below: Join the conversation! title: Anything Can Happen: There is still no update on Packers’ Josh Jacobs
summary: It has been nearly three months since Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs was arrested on charges of felony strangulation and several other misdemeanors related to domestic abuse. That’s also just about how long it’s been since we last had an update from the team, the league, or law enforcement officials. Jacobs has said via […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers looks on during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images It has been nearly three months since Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs was arrested on charges of felony strangulation and several other misdemeanors related to domestic abuse. That’s also just about how long it’s been since we last had an update from the team, the league, or law enforcement officials. Jacobs has said via his lawyers that he “vehemently denies the allegations”. HC Matt LaFleur echoed the team’s initial statement, saying they would let the process play out. Aaaaand, now we’re in the back half of August. The NFL’s first round of player suspensions was recently announced, most notably: Atlanta Falcons DE James Pearce, who was suspended 8 games after his February arrest on domestic violence charges which included stalking and aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. No suspension was announced for Jacobs, likely because things are still under investigation. If or when things finally start moving again, I don’t have high hopes that the league will respond in a way I deem appropriate. After all, stalking and aggravated battery get you 8 games. Holding a gun to someone’s head will cost you 5 games. Sometimes domestic violence incidents get you suspended for 6 games . Or 4 games. But hey! Sometimes domestic violence does get you kicked out of the league , but I suspect that’s only if you’re not very good at your job. Pretty soon they’re going to let players spin a big wheel to decide their fate just like on The Price is Right . Back to Josh Jacobs. With the most recent update being that there…is no update, ESPN’s Adam Schefter says that a suspension for Jacobs is still on the table. As evidenced by the examples above, it’s looking like Jacobs could be facing a punishment anywhere from a 1 game suspension to being completely banned from the league. The NFL just doesn’t know.

title: Packers claim edge rusher Arden Walker, fill roster
summary: Several days after the Green Bay Packers opened up a roster spot by waiving quarterback Kyron Drones, the team finally filled the position today by claiming pass-rusher Arden Walker off waivers. Walker, an undrafted rookie, was waived by the Minnesota Vikings — who also run a 3-4 defense — after the team replaced Walker with […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 12: Arden Walker #53 of the Colorado Buffaloes gestures during the first half against the Houston Cougars at TDECU Stadium on September 12, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Several days after the Green Bay Packers opened up a roster spot by waiving quarterback Kyron Drones , the team finally filled the position today by claiming pass-rusher Arden Walker off waivers. Walker, an undrafted rookie, was waived by the Minnesota Vikings — who also run a 3-4 defense — after the team replaced Walker with former UFL edge defender Kenny Dyson yesterday. Walker is a relatively unknown prospect, as he was not one of the 2,700+ players ranked by The Athletic’s Dane Brugler in his “ The Beast ” series. Walker also only signed with the Vikings for $2,000 in guaranteed money following the draft, which is significantly less than any of the UDFAs the Packers signed immediately after the draft . For perspective, edge rusher Nyjalik Kelly received $262,500 in guarantees when he signed with Green Bay. According to NFL Pro , Walker played 18 snaps in the Vikings’ preseason opener last week, first appearing in the game with two seconds left in the third quarter. 17 of those 18 snaps came on defense, with the other coming on special teams. Below are some highlights from Walker during his college days at Colorado: Arden Walker (6’2 250) Colorado + Team leader/captain + 28.0% win rate on true pass sets during the 2025 season + Durable player that has played over 1,300 career snaps + 8.8% missed tackle rate in 2024 + 72.1 pass rush grade in 2025 + Natural leverage – 8 career sacks -… pic.twitter.com/Ct4JDEUkBJ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) April 4, 2026 Per NFL Draft Scout , Walker, who was a non-combine invite, measured in at 6’2”-flat and 242 pounds at Colorado’s pro day. There, he ran a 4.78-second 40-yard dash, a 7.20-second three-cone drill and had a 31” vertical jump. Walker began his career at Missouri as a backup before transferring to Colorado, where he played his final three years. He was a full-time starter in only his senior season. There could be two reasons why the Packers might want to add at the edge rusher position right now. First, Dani Dennis-Sutton, Green Bay’s fourth-round rookie, is going into his second week of missing practice with an illness. Second, the aforementioned Kelly has been missing practice with a knee injury. At the moment, we don’t know the severity of Kelly’s knee injury.

title: Packers Training Camp Recap: Cornerback competition ramps up
summary: Obviously, cornerback Keisean Nixon generated some buzz on Sunday after he told the press that he guesses he’s “being punished right now” by working occasionally with the second-team defense, and stayed on the field with both the first- and second-team defenses throughout the Green Bay Packers’ preseason opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Head coach Matt […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Keisean Nixon #25 of the Green Bay Packers in action during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Obviously, cornerback Keisean Nixon generated some buzz on Sunday after he told the press that he guesses he’s “being punished right now” by working occasionally with the second-team defense, and stayed on the field with both the first- and second-team defenses throughout the Green Bay Packers’ preseason opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Head coach Matt LaFleur addressed the situation in his pre-practice press conference on Tuesday, joking, “He loves making a headline, doesn’t he,” with a smile on his face. When asked about how he feels about Nixon as a player and a person, LaFleur stated, “I love Kei. He’s been awesome since the day he got here.” As far as how the head coach would handle the words his projected starting cornerback made, LaFleur responded, “I’m not gonna micro-manage everything that everybody says.” LaFleur said that every spot on the team is a competition, which has been the company line for the Packers throughout training camp. Today, though, it seemed like the cornerback rotation opened up more than it had in the past, which we’ll cover in our defensive notes in this article. Before we get into what happened at practice today, LaFleur said two other notable things, in terms of the mechanics of the preseason. First, he stated that offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich called the offensive plays against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Usually, LaFleur has given coordinators and assistants one quarter each to call plays in previous preseason games. Second, LaFleur also stated that the current plan right now is for the starters to play two drives against the Denver Broncos, compared to the one they played against the Steelers, in Week 2. In Week 3, the team hopes to use joint practices against the Arizona Cardinals to get reps for the first-team units, and let the backups play the actual preseason game. So it seems like quarterback Jordan Love will make two appearances in the preseason this year, both on the road, but won’t have a helmet on for the home preseason game. Unless you caught him on Family Night, the first time you’re going to get to see Love throw at Lambeau Field in-person this year will be on Thursday Night Football in Week 3 (September 24th) against the Atlanta Falcons. Injuries Four players remain on the Packers’ physically unable to perform list: tight end Luke Musgrave (neck), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (ankle), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee) and long snapper Matt Orzech (calf). On Tuesday, general manager Brian Gutekunst hinted that Orzech could be returning to practice within the next week or so, but the expectation is still for both Riley and Parsons, who seem to be recovering well from their season-ending injuries from last year, to start on the PUP list to begin the regular season. Musgrave is the wild card. Players who returned to practice today were running back Josh Jacobs (groin) and edge defender Lukas Van Ness (shoulder). Van Ness played in the preseason opener and missed just one practice with his shoulder issue, while Jacobs has been out a while with his groin injury. Players who remain out of practice are offensive lineman Darian Kinnard (ankle), edge defender Dani Dennis-Sutton (illness), edge defender Nyjalik Kelly (knee) and safety Javon Bullard (foot). The Packers are on record that Kinnard, Dennis-Sutton and Bullard won’t be out long-term, but they haven’t commented (or been asked) about Kelly. Offense Even with Aaron Banks returning to team drills for the first time in training camp, he did not immediately hop back into the first-team line as the full-time left guard, as the starting line today was: Jordan Morgan, Jager Burton, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Zach Bako-Bewele (left to right). Yes, that means Anthony Belton is still on the bench, despite Bako-Bewele returning to the full-time right tackle role after missing team drills for most of camp. This could be a byproduct of the team being down Darian Kinnard, one of the few backup “true tackles” that the team has on the second line of the depth chart, but we’ll have to see how this evolves moving forward. Generally, Belton spent most of the early portion of the offseason at guard, where he performed better than tackle last year and eventually developed into a starter midway through the season, and has now spent almost all of his time at tackle as of lately. Tomorrow, we’re going to run a breakdown of Burton and Monk’s performances during their extended look in the preseason opener, including video from the game, so you guys can get a look at the Packers’ potential Week 1 guards. Bank did rotate in at left guard in place of Burton at times during practice on Tuesday. Oh Mylanta, Tucker Kraft just went all David Tyree against Keisean Nixon for an amazing one-handed grab against his helmet. — Dave Schroeder (@SchroederWBAY) August 18, 2026 The play of the day was quarterback Jordan Love chucking it to tight end Tucker Kraft, who just returned to team drills yesterday, as he caught a one-handed ball against his helmet after running up the seam in double coverage. I’m not worried about Kraft losing a step post-injury. Receiver Bo Melton dropped out of practice late today, as he was shaken up on a deep shot in double coverage and returned to the field without a jersey or helmet after talking to trainers. Defense Before practice, Gutekunst praised the defensive line room, stating that they have “more than enough. That’s unusual.” Javon Hargrave returned to team drills for the first time all camp after starting on the PUP list, but it was Karl Brooks and Devonte Wyatt who were the starters in the team’s first-look nickel defense. Again, this shouldn’t be too surprising, as Green Bay protected Brooks like an entrenched starter in the preseason opener and listed Brooks as a starting defensive tackle on their unofficial depth chart , which has basically been accurate outside of the guard position. Starters: Love Brooks Golden – Watson Kraft – Whyle Morgan – Burton – Rhyan – Monk – ZBB LVN – Brooks – Wyatt – Sorrell Coop – Zaire Nixon – Cisse Oladapo – Williams X Aaron Banks getting team reps at RG but worked behind Burton 👀 — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 18, 2026 Hargrave did get some looks with the 1s today, though. Obviously, the defensive line will rotate a lot. The run line is Wyatt, Ford at nose and Brooks. — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) August 18, 2026 Note: Jonathan Ford, who is played specifically as a head-up nose tackle for the team, but received snaps with the first- through third-team units in the Packers’ preseason opener, did get some looks with the first-team defense again in practice. It’s going to be interesting to see how Green Bay decides who will be the team’s sixth (and likely last) interior defensive lineman, a race that will come down to Ford, Nazir Stackhouse and camp riser Anthony Campbell. In the slot, safety Kitan Oladapo, who is stepping up as the injury replacement to Javon Bullard (following the waiving of injured Johnathan Baldwin), started with the first-team unit. Oladapo has looked much more comfortable at safety in his time in the NFL than in the slot, where we got his first extended look at that position against the Steelers on Thursday. kamal Hadden playing nickel with ones — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) August 18, 2026 Another slot option that the Packers have is cornerback Kamal Hadden, who worked with the safeties today (the safeties have generally played the slot in Green Bay in recent years). Hadden (ankle), Carrington Valentine (hamstring) and Domani Jackson (core) were all held out of the preseason opener, leaving the Packers down three of their top six cornerbacks going into the game. All three of those corners were involved in team periods…

title: Green Bay Packers News: What does the Packers’ future look like?
summary: As the Packers head toward the end of training camp, let’s spare a thought for the future of the team. What will they look like in 2027 and beyond? Assuming Tucker Kraft’s extension is as done of a deal as everyone seems to think, pretty much every player of consequence is already locked in for […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 10: Xavier McKinney #29 of the Green Bay Packers reacts during an NFL wild card playoff game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the Packers head toward the end of training camp, let’s spare a thought for the future of the team. What will they look like in 2027 and beyond? Assuming Tucker Kraft’s extension is as done of a deal as everyone seems to think, pretty much every player of consequence is already locked in for next season. Keisean Nixon is the only significant starter (depending what you think of Karl Brooks as both a starter and a significant player) who is currently slated to hit free agency. But other notable names, even if they’re not starters, are scheduled to be free agents, including Darian Kinnard, Luke Musgrave, the aforementioned Karl Brooks, and Carrington Valentine, among others. There are significant decisions to be made there. And that’s not even counting the guys who are under contract for next season, but maybe shouldn’t be — guys like Aaron Banks and Josh Jacobs, just to name two. These, too, are significant decision points and will shape what the Packers are able to do in free agency next spring and beyond. But by and large, the Packers look like they’re in pretty solid shape. They’ve had a couple of solid drafts lately, they have a good core of established veterans, and with a couple of the annual roster tweaks you’d expect from any NFL team trying to contend, they’ll be in the mix for years to come.
