title: What we've seen from Travis Hunter at Jaguars training camp
summary: Hunter is almost through his second NFL training camp. What has stood out from his split time at receiver and cornerback?
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- For the first time in training camp, the  Jacksonville Jaguars  limited Travis Hunter to one side of the ball in 11-on-11 work.

 Hunter played exclusively at cornerback Monday, getting on the field for 20 of the 24 snaps. Coach Liam Coen said the move was done to allow Hunter to focus more on playing without missing any mental reps when switching to offense. 

 "When he's not in [on defense] and he's coming [onto] offense every time, we're losing out on even more coaching in those moments," Coen said. "And so wanted to just be very intentional today about getting him some of those visual reps so [defensive pass game coordinator Matt Araujo] can coach him even when he's not in [on defense]. He's not running over [to switch to offense]. So we just wanted to get him a little bit more of that."

 The 20 defensive snaps were the most Hunter has played on defense in a training camp practice, excluding last week's joint practice in New Orleans. Hunter, who did play five offensive snaps in the 7-on-7 period Monday, said he welcomed the extra work.

 

 "It's definitely beneficial," he said. "I needed to knock the rest off. I've got to get better somehow, somewhere, so I definitely took my time to hone in on [the] defensive [side], get better, get my feet up under me.

 "Can't let nobody catch the ball. That's my motto right now, just continue to focus and get better."

 Hunter has been on the field in 11-on-11 for 178 snaps so far in camp (minus the joint practice): 116 on defense, 61 on offense and one on special teams. Veteran cornerback Jourdan Lewis is still amazed when watching him play on both sides of the ball.

 "I told him he's a beast, man," Lewis said. "You've got camp two times, man, because you have to do it as a receiver and a corner, and I think he's handled it really well."

 As the Jaguars prepare for their second preseason game  Friday, here are three other takeaways from Hunter's second training camp in the pros:

 

 Hunter has 'elite ball skills' 
 Defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said Hunter, who has two interceptions in 11-on-11 so far in camp, has "elite ball skills." One takeaway came on a leaping snag of  Trevor Lawrence 's pass to Parker Washington on the goal line. The play was pretty much dead on a likely sack, but Lawrence threw the ball up anyway and Hunter came running in from the middle of the field for the interception.

 "The thing about Travis, you can see even in some of these practices, he can go up and tear the ball out of the air," Campanile said. "He goes after the ball like a receiver, so that's what's exciting about him. And you saw a little bit of that in practice the other day. I thought he made a heck of a play, honestly, coming out of nowhere and tearing the ball out of the sky."

 Coen described it this way: "Travis just came out of nowhere and makes the play. Like, I can't coach it [the ability to make plays like that]."

 On the first day of camp, Hunter broke up one and almost came down with a twisting, leaping catch on a Lawrence throw that was behind him. His body control to even get a hand on that throw was reminiscent of the body-contorting catches he had against the 49ers and Chiefs  last season.

 "When he has the ball in his hands, he can create something special," wide receiver  Jakobi Meyers  said. "He can make guys miss. He has a great awareness of defenders and space out there on the field, but he also has great ball skills. So those things kind of pop off the tape."

 

 He hasn't been targeted on defense a lot 
 One play from Monday's practice perfectly illustrates why Hunter hasn't been targeted a lot. Hunter had wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr . in man coverage, locking him up from the moment Thomas left the line of scrimmage. So Lawrence took a quick look Thomas' way then went elsewhere.

 It's not like the Jaguars' quarterbacks are completely avoiding him, as Washington beat Hunter off the sideline for a deep touchdown pass last week. On Monday, Lawrence threw twice to a receiver Hunter was guarding. He knocked down a pass intended for  CJ Williams , but he allowed Tim Jones to catch a short pass on the other.

 "When you have length and anticipation and have a good feel for routes, I think that the playmaking, getting your hands on balls or just denying the ball with good coverage, that's a win in itself that I think goes a little bit unnoticed from corners," Coen said. "It's like, yeah, when they don't get a lot of work, it's probably because they're doing their job and doing it at a high level, so I've been pleased with him."

 

 

 Hunter and Thomas are sharing reps 
 As expected, Hunter is being used in some packages as the third receiver.

 Washington and Meyers have been getting the most snaps of the receivers in camp -- even though Thomas was arguably the best player on the field in the spring and has had a great camp, showing some of the toughness and ball security that seemed to be missing last season.

 Coen likes using 12 personnel (one running back, two tight ends and two receivers), and the Jaguars are reluctant to put Washington on the sideline. When the Jaguars use 11 personnel (one back, one tight end and three receivers), Hunter and Thomas have shared reps.

 That doesn't mean Hunter and Thomas won't be on the field together once the season begins, but it's a little hint as to how this full receiver room will shake out. And while Coen hasn't announced their exact offensive plan for Hunter, the coach did hint that it could be bigger than some might expect.

 "We all know he's our 3A, 3B receiver right now, and [we're] trying to get him the exposure to every opportunity that we have out here," Coen said. "But right now, I mean, we need a lot of the communication, a lot of the repetition needs to continue obviously on both sides of the ball."

 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Chiefs stories 
 
 Chiefs' Bieniemy: Wife to make full recovery after being shot 
 Rookie Benson earns shot to start at RT for Chiefs 
 Tight end Travis Kelce says he can still 'play at a high level' 
 Reid: Mahomes unlikely to play in preseason opener 
 Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen an early star of Chiefs training camp 
 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 

 Day after day, the Chiefs' injuries continue to pile up. For the first time in camp, left tackle Josh Simmons missed Tuesday's practice because of a back injury.

 Receivers Tyquan Thornton (strained hamstring) and Jimmy Holiday (quad) left practice early as well. Earlier during Tuesday's on-field work, defensive end Ashton Gillotte , who returned just two days ago following a strained hamstring, sustained a right foot injury while covering tight end Jared Wiley . Linebacker Jack Cochrane missed Tuesday's work with a right knee injury.

 Those players were added to a list that already includes safety Chamarri Conner (sore knee), right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerbacks L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and Kader Kohou (sore ankle), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) who have been held out of practice for much of the past week.

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 Wearing the usual white jersey for defenders, Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane fully participated in Monday's practice for the first time since camp started.

 Delane missed Saturday's preseason opener as the Chiefs held him out while he continued to let his right shoulder heal, an injury that had led him to wear a noncontact yellow jersey and miss the 11-on-11 reps. In Monday's work, Delane did well to cover receivers such as Rashee Rice , Nikko Remigio and rookie Cyrus Allen . If Delane continues progressing this week, he should make his preseason debut Saturday when the Chiefs face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 "He did everything and was in all the drills," coach Andy Reid said of Delane. "[He] looked good, so that's good work for him as he goes through that. We'll just monitor him and see how he does with the extended play."

 More observations: 

 
 Monday's practice was the Chiefs' longest of camp -- a session that lasted two hours and 15 minutes. Reid said backup left tackle Esa Pole left practice early because he was dehydrated. Receiver Andrew Armstrong sustained a strained hamstring, linebacker Jack Cochrane left early with a knee injury, and undrafted rookie safety DeShon Singleton tweaked a hamstring. 
 Missing practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms), safety Chamarri Conner (knee) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). "Trey is doing [well]," Reid said. "He's getting close. We'll see where it goes. I don't know if you'll see him this week, but he's getting close. 
 The lone major lineup change among the projected starters was along the offensive line. Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, switched from right guard -- the position he played in Saturday's preseason loss to the Los Angeles Rams -- to right tackle. Jaylon Moore , a five-year veteran, switched from right tackle to right guard, the spot where Smith starts. Reid suggested that Benson was moved to get him ready to play the right tackle position in Saturday's exhibition against the Buccaneers. "Moore has been doing a great job in there for us," Reid said. "With that, Benson doesn't get any reps at [right tackle]. We want him to go against the better players and have a chance to continue to grow there. We just flopped them over and let Moore get some reps at guard and Benson gets some reps at the tackle spot. Benson held his own at the guard spot in the game. They need to be able to play both [positions]. It's good experience for them." 
 

 

 

 Who has been the Chiefs' top performer so far at camp? 
 Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods has been a revelation. Not only has the first-round pick made an impact in each practice, but Woods has quickly shown that he has the quickness and strength to be a potential impact player next to pass rusher Chris Jones . Veterans including center Creed Humphrey , right guard Trey Smith and defensive end George Karlaftis  have praised Woods throughout camp.

 Woods' explosive ability has helped him produce highlight moments in the trenches, whether blowing by Humphrey on a running play or showing off his pass-rush skills in one-on-one drills. Just last week, the 6-foot-3, 310-pound Woods sprinted to chase down Patrick Mahomes , impressing the quarterback.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 The lone major position battle is at the right tackle position. Coach Andy Reid is eager to see how Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, performs in the preseason.

 The Chiefs have given Benson most of the first-team reps, hoping he can provide true competition to Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran. If Benson continues to overachieve, even in the preseason -- especially since he's expected to play snaps at right tackle and right guard -- the Chiefs will have to decide if they feel comfortable with him protecting  Patrick Mahomes  despite not having any NFL experience.

 Moore is the safer option, but Benson should have plenty of snaps to demonstrate that he's ready for the spotlight that is opening night on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos on "Monday Night Football."

 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 As expected, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Thursday that quarterback Patrick Mahomes will not play in the preseason opener Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams . Reid said the decision to not play Mahomes is a precautionary measure since the quarterback is still recovering from the surgery he had in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in left knee.

 "It'll be Justin [Fields] and then Garrett [Nussmeier] and then Chris [Oladokun] will take it from there," Reid said of Saturday's quarterback rotation. "We'll just see how the reps go as we work through that."

 Without Mahomes, Reid could decide to not play several starters against the Rams, a decision that would be different from previous years. One of those veterans who requested to not be in uniform was pass rusher Chris Jones , the defense's longest-tenured member.

 "Why play the starters?" Jones said. "I mean, it's so much risk you're taking to play the starters in the preseason. I hope Coach Reid [will] be like, 'You know what, starters don't play.'"

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Thursday's practice were safety Chamarri Conner (sore knee), right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerbacks L'Jarius Sneed (rest) and Kader Kohou (sore ankle), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 Although he wasn't selected in the NFL draft, Chiefs rookie right tackle Kahlil Benson was confident he'd be able to compete for a roster spot. Benson, however, has impressed the Chiefs enough so far into their training camp that he has a chance to win a starting spot on the offensive line. Benson will get his opportunity to make a strong first impression Saturday when…

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Patriots' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 Patriots TE Hunter Henry signs extension worth up to $20M 
 Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice? 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 18 
 Former Patriots wide receiver Julian Edelman was a guest of the team's light, low-tempo practice. Edelman watched from the sideline and at one point was chatting with owner Robert Kraft.

 "It's always good to have Patriots legends around here," veteran tight end Hunter Henry said. "The more the merrier. Those guys set the standard here, so it's always good to have them back."

 Edelman also caught up with wide receiver A.J. Brown , who will be under the spotlight the next two days with the Eagles coming to town for two practices. Edelman had given Brown his blessing to wear his old No. 11, but Brown previously said he wanted to honor Edelman's legacy and create his own by wearing No. 1 (his old college number).

 

 More observations: 

 
 The Patriots officially signed veteran G/C Greg Van Roten to a one-year deal and released TE Mitch Van Vooren . The 36-year-old Van Roten, who projects as the top interior backup with Ben Brown sidelined multiple weeks due to injury, has been assigned jersey No. 70. 
 Veteran LB Robert Spillane was one of the last players on the field after practice, as he spent time working with 2026 second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas on punt protection and punt-rush technique. 
 As for what to expect in Wednesday and Thursday practices with the Eagles, coach Mike Vrabel said: "I think upwards of probably 28 reps, 30 reps for the first group on each day is a good number ... we'll be able to do a lot more field work on the first day and then probably focus on the red zone the next day." 
 The Patriots had veteran free agent DT DaQuan Jones and veteran free agent LB Shaq Thompson in for visits (different from tryouts). 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 17 
 Quarterback Drake Maye  delivered a beautiful deep pass to receiver A.J. Brown for a 65-yard(ish) touchdown over the middle, which was the highlight play of practice.

 Maye thrust his right arm into the air in celebration, with his right index finger extended. A few yards behind him, coach Mike Vrabel did the same.

 The play, and celebration, served as a fitting preview for what is to come: Brown's former team, the Eagles, visiting New England for practice on Wednesday and Thursday. Brown is scheduled to address reporters after Wednesday's practice.

 Maye and Brown have been working behind the scenes, and on the field, to develop a connection. Their lockers are next to each other. Brown also said they often sit next to each other in meetings.

 Some of their best work leading into Monday has been in the red zone, where Brown's size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) and physicality have shown up. They hadn't experienced consistent success on the deep ball before Monday, which might have explained the emphatic reactions from Maye and Vrabel.

 More observations: 

 
 In a rare drill that fourth-year DT Cory Durden said he's never seen before in the NFL, the team gathered on one field and rookies and first-year players were challenged to one-on-one drills as everyone watched. One highlight was first-round pick Caleb Lomu (right tackle) blocking second-round pick Gabe Jacas (outside linebacker). "Coach was giving them an opportunity to perform in front of their teammates. It's a pride thing," Durden said. "It brings energy to everybody. Nobody wants to lose in front of the whole team." 
 Kicker Andy Borregales was once again challenged in a full-team field goal drill by kicking into skinny posts (about half the width of regulation goal posts). Two days after going 6-of-6, he was 3-of-5 from a distance between 37 and 52 yards. The two misses were estimated to have been successful on regular goalposts. 
 Starting LB Christian Elliss and reserve OLB Jesse Luketa left the full-pads practice early, while starting DT Christian Barmore returned. 
 CB Christian Gonzalez has remained out of practice since appearing to injure his ankle Aug. 12. 
 

 

 
 Who has been the Patriots' top performer at camp so far? 
 CB Christian Gonzalez . The question entering training camp was if he might be a hold-in due to ongoing talks on a contract extension. Instead, he was a full participant the first 13 practices and played a significant role in elevating the competition level for the entire team with his back-and-forth, fire-breathing one-on-one matchup with WR A.J. Brown -- which was arguably the top storyline of camp.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How much is the rookie class ready to contribute? First-round pick Caleb Lomu ideally projects as the swing offensive tackle, second-round pick Gabe Jacas as a top backup OLB who creates havoc as a pass rusher, and third-round pick Eli Raridon as the No. 2 tight end behind Hunter Henry . Their performance in games can solidify those roles, along with other rookie-based questions, such as whether seventh-round pick Behren Morton earns a roster spot as the No. 3 quarterback.

 

 Saturday, Aug. 15 
 Two days after Andy Borregales was 2-of-5 on field goal attempts in the preseason opener, he was put in a pressure-filled spot by coach Mike Vrabel in practice Saturday.

 Borregales had to kick through skinny goalposts that are about half the width of regulation goalposts. He aced the test, going 6-of-6 from a distance between 32 and 47 yards.

 "Obviously, the skinny posts are posed as a challenge after the game," Borregales said after the practice attended by season-ticket holders. "At the end of the day, whatever two poles are in front of me, that's my target and that's my job that I have to do.

 "I felt like I bounced back today, going back to the basics."

 After Thursday's 13-13 tie with the Colts, in which Borregales was wide left from 56, 55 and 49 yards, the second-year kicker said he planned to watch the tape and make improvements. The miss from 49 came at the end of regulation.

 What did he learn?

 "Just some technical stuff. I came out here today and fixed those little issues," he said. "I think today was a great day to build off."

 One change that also might have helped was the return of incumbent snapper Julian Ashby , who missed the last week with an ankle injury.

 More observations: 

 
 Top backup center/guard Ben Brown , who was knocked out of the preseason opener with an undisclosed lower-body injury, will miss multiple weeks throughout the preseason, according to Vrabel. 
 Another top backup center/guard, Andrew Rupcich , also didn't finish the preseason opener after appearing get rolled up on. He didn't practice Saturday. The injuries to Brown and Rupcich led the team to sign free agent interior offensive linemen Darrian Dalcourt (Alabama) and Joe Michalski (Oklahoma State). 
 WR Romeo Doubs delivered multiple highlight-reel touchdown catches, including one in the end zone over CB Charles Woods to cap off a red zone drill. Doubs threw the football high…

title: 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Giants training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Giants' top camp performer and biggest lingering question.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 Giants' Malik Nabers 'felt good' in 1st full-speed live drills 
 Giants QB Jaxson Dart 'puzzled' by latest concussion test request 
 A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp -- an inside look 
 QB Jaxson Dart lauded for inbounds slide at Giants camp 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 

 Malik Nabers participated in full live-speed team drills for the second straight day in a red jersey. And he looked even better than he did on Monday.

 Nabers saw a slightly increased workload. He ran eight routes and caught four passes from quarterback Jaxson Dart in 11-on-11 and 7-on-7 drills. Of course, it helped that the defense couldn't touch him.

 On one deep pass, safeties Jevon Holland and Tyler Nubin had to pull up on the play to avoid any contact.

 Coach John Harbaugh said that Nabers "handled it well" bouncing back after his first day of live drills. The next step is adding reps, getting bumped around, shedding the red jersey and feeling contact. That could come as early as next week.

 In the meantime, Nabers' workload will be light during Thursday's joint practice with the Dolphins. Barring a setback, the expectation seems to be that Nabers will be ready for Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys .

 

 More observations: 

 
 Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr . was first up at running back on Tuesday. He's still squarely in the Giants plans even with the signing of Najee Harris . Tracy and Cam Skattebo have both been the first running back up throughout training camp. 
 Harbaugh seemed to indicate he expects it to take a "couple weeks" before Harris gets into football shape. The veteran running back did only individual drills on Tuesday. 
 The Giants worked on a lot of red zone and short-yardage situations on Tuesday. Dart's running was a big part of the practice. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 
 The referee at practice threw a flag on Colton Hood after he cut off wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr . in the end zone. The rookie cornerback didn't like the call and made it known.

 Coach John Harbaugh saw it unfold. He didn't agree with Hood's assessment and sent him to the sideline. But not until they had a quick chat.

 "I wasn't angry. I just wanted to make the point that, you know, what are you arguing about?" Harbaugh said. "The ball was in the air and you pushed the receiver and redirected him. It was a restriction. That's going to be pass interference. But he's competitive. He's competitive. He wants to win every snap. And I think [that's] part of the journey for the young corners."

 Hood had his ups and downs in the preseason opener -- a 13-10 loss against the Minnesota Vikings . And again at Monday's practice. Harbaugh said Hood was going to be playing plenty and just wanted to accelerate the learning curve.

 Hopefully this was a lesson learned.

 More observations: 

 

 

 Who is the Giants' top performer so far at camp? 
 TE Isaiah Likely  The offseason acquisition has been the Giants' No. 1 receiver with Malik Nabers not participating in team drills. He's been quarterback  Jaxson Dart 's safety net, leading all first-team receivers in catches by a wide margin.

 "Zay's done a great job," offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said.

 The way Likely smoothly gets in and out of breaks has just looked different from incumbent starter Theo Johnson . He also seems to have the best handle on the new offense given his familiarity with coach John Harbaugh and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman from Baltimore. Given the way Dart likes to throw to his tight ends, it suggests that Likely is in for a breakout season given the chemistry they already have developed.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Can the offense put it together? There are a lot of things working against Dart early in camp. He's learning a new offense, doesn't have Nabers in live drills and the structure of practice prohibits endless freelancing, which is perhaps what he does best. So it has been a struggle.

 The offense has failed to put together many big days in practice throughout the summer. Nagy said they expected there to be "highs and lows through this process" for their young quarterback. To see Dart and the first-team offense have some success in the preseason, even if it's just flashes, would be a welcome sight and could provide a confidence boost entering the season.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 The Giants are working hard at training camp. There is no doubt about that. Even on a rare day when they weren't in pads and ran a mental-rep practice that resembled a walk-through, coach John Harbaugh had the Giants on the field for two-plus hours.

 The practice concluded with them going over pregame introductions and the new routine for warmups. Every detail is important at the difficult Camp Harbaugh, which had players in full pads at seven of the past 10 practices.

 "My toughest training camp in 10 years," said fullback Patrick Ricard , who came over from Baltimore with Harbaugh.

 In a way, this has reminded some Giants of a college camp. With fewer rules, the big school colleges are known to run much harder and longer practices than the NFL.

 "I was with another Harbaugh [Jim Harbaugh at Michigan] for five years and it seems very similar to that," guard Jon Runyan  said.

 Now the Giants will see if it leads to better results.

 

 More observations: 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 The kicking competition continues: Ben Sauls went 5-of-6 on field goal attempts in Wednesday's practice. Rookie Dominic Zvada went 7-of-7, including a 61-yarder to end practice.

 Overall in camp, Zvada is now 48-of-51 on kicks. Sauls is 41-of-48.

 "They're both having really good camps," coach John Harbaugh said.

 Running back Cam Skattebo and tight end Isaiah Likely peer-pressured Harbaugh into having Zvada attempt the 61-yard kick after the offense repeatedly sputtered in end-of-game situations. There were 10 seconds remaining on the clock and Harbaugh had the offense out on the field ready to run a play from the 44-yard line.

 He reconsidered. Zvada drilled the kick with plenty of room to spare (it clanked off the back fence) as the offense went wild.

 At this point, it seems a fait accompli that the Giants will carry a kicker with little to no experience come Week 1.

 More observations:  

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 It was another rough afternoon for the Giants' offense. The unit sputtered and failed to hit any downfield throws during a practice without full pads.

 During one red zone drill, quarterback Jaxson Dart threw touchdown passes to Theo Johnson and Malachi Fields on two of the first three plays. He followed with five straight incompletions, including an interception at the goal line by Arvell Reese .

 These are the learning curves with a new offense.

 "[Tuesday] was an average practice, maybe below average," offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said. "It wasn't good enough. [Dart] knows that, we know that. We'll put it on tape, but we also talk about success through struggles and ... there's going to be some struggles as we go through this now in training camp and during the season. But how do we react?"

 The season starts in just over a month. The Giants are combining the offenses of Nagy, quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan…

title: 2026 New York Jets training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Jets training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Jets reporter Rich Cimini has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jets camp. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Jets' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jets camp 
 
 RB Breece Hall strains groin, Glenn says its not serious 
 Jets CB Stiggers taken to hospital after collapsing at practice 
 No. 2 pick Bailey living up to hype, bringing 'juice' to Jets 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq to miss time after hernia setback 
 Jets' Smith rues being 'distraction' after dispute with girlfriend 
 2026 Jets training camp preview 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 

 Quarterback Geno Smith , learning a new system, said it's "very important" for him to play in the preseason. But he wouldn't take it further, saying the decision belongs to coach Aaron Glenn.

 Smith is dealing with a sore left ankle. He hasn't missed any practice time, but he was scratched from the preseason opener last Friday. On Tuesday, Glenn was noncommittal on whether Smith would play Friday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers .

 Every other offensive starter played last week. Ideally, Smith would get a couple of series against the Steelers for the sake of timing and chemistry.

 Smith is accustomed to playing in the preseason. He played 28 snaps last summer for the Las Vegas Raiders . In his final two preseasons with the Seattle Seahawks , 2023 and 2024, he played a combined total of only 17 snaps.

 "I'll leave it up to coach, but my job is to get ready and help this team get ready to be ready to play Week 1," Smith said. "Whenever I get the chance to play, I look forward to it. I'll also leave that up to coach."

 Smith, commenting for the first time on his ankle injury, was tightlipped. He wouldn't say how it happened, except to say, "I just had some swelling, swelling in my ankle." It developed during last week's joint practices with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 For what it's worth, the sleeve on his lower left leg was gone for practice.

 Other observations:  

 
 Rookie QB Cade Klubnik threw a couple of interceptions in practice, one on a pass that was tipped by Will McDonald IV and picked off by Azareye'h Thomas and another on a ball that was dropped by Chip Trayanum and intercepted by  Samuel Womack III . 
 With the injuries to Breece Hall (groin) and Isaiah Davis (knee), Trayanum and Sam Scott -- both rookie free agents -- are getting extra reps. Scott, out of Wyoming, has had some impressive moments. 
 A handful of Jets' legends watched practice, including Vinny Testaverde, Kevin Mawae and Keyshawn Johnson -- members of the 1998 team that reached the AFC Championship Game. 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq (hernia) and rookie CB D'Angelo Ponds (calf) are inching closer to returning. They're expected to be ready for Week 1, according to Glenn. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 It was a rough way to end practice.

 RB Breece Hall was in the locker room, nursing a groin injury from earlier in practice. WR Garrett Wilson was nowhere to be found; he showed up sick in the morning, vomiting, and was held out. QB Geno Smith was on the field, taking his full share of reps, but he was favoring his left ankle -- an injury that occurred Wednesday and kept him out of the preseason opener Friday.

 Not a great day for the Jets' big three on offense.

 Smith powered through the relatively light practice, though he did have one hiccup -- an overthrow that was picked off by S Andre Cisco in a two-minute drill.

 Coach Aaron Glenn acknowledged that Smith still is feeling the residual effects of the injury, adding, "I want to see exactly how he feels coming out of this practice to see how we're going to continue to move forward."

 Something to watch. Rookie Cade Klubnik started the opener and played well.

 Other observations:  

 
 There was some positive injury news, as NT T'Vondre Sweat and edge  Joseph Ossai practiced for the first time. Both are projected starters. "We want to make sure we take our time with [Sweat]," Glenn said of the 360-pounder. 
 The cornerback room has absorbed some hits. Nahshon Wright (undisclosed), Qwan'tez Stiggers (concussion) and rookie D'Angelo Ponds (calf) didn't practice. Ponds, who was expected to compete for a starting job, still hasn't practiced. Rookie free agent Mory Bamba , who recorded four passes defensed in the opener, injured a knee in the game and will be sidelined at least two weeks. 
 WRs Isaiah Williams and rookie Omar Cooper Jr . stayed after practice for about an hour, each catching about 100 balls from the JUGS machine. They also caught tennis balls and bean bags. Williams, known for his kickoff and punt return abilities, said he wants to improve his hands. 
 Despite two consecutive days with no practice, LB  Demario Davis  and S Minkah Fitzpatrick received veteran rest days. Load management is one of the themes in camp. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13  
 
 Who has been the Jets' top performer so far at camp? 

 Let's go with a rookie -- edge rusher David Bailey , the No. 2 overall pick. Those who criticized the Jets for drafting Bailey over LB Arvell Reese have been quiet lately. As a pass rusher, Bailey has been dominant at times, demonstrating elite first-step quickness. In joint practices with the Bucs, he caused a lot of problems for veteran RT Luke Goedeke , a $22 million-a-year player. Bailey still has to answer questions as a run defender -- he must clean up some technique stuff -- but his speed off the edge will make him a fun watch in 2026. 

 "He looks like he's everything that was advertised -- and more," MLB Demario Davis said.

 
 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 Can Geno Smith and the passing game get off the ground? They added some weapons, drafting TE Kenyon Sadiq and WR Omar Cooper Jr . in the first round, but this has been a slow-go for Smith & Co. On some days, Smith looks fantastic. Other days, not so much. Look, no one expects immediate success, but there should be incremental progress -- which is why the preseason games are so important. All told, the starters are expected to play 25 to 30 snaps. Another player (WR Adonai Mitchell ?) needs to step up as the No. 2 option, behind Garrett Wilson . That'll make it easier for Smith.

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 Baker Mayfield beat the Jets with a two-minute drill last season in Week 3, setting up a game-winning field goal for the Buccaneers as time expired, and he did it again on Wednesday in the second of two joint practices.

 The Bucs' QB burned the Jets with three straight completions, hitting Dennis Houston with a short TD pass with three seconds left in a two-minute drill.

 "Baker does a really good job in that situation, and I wanted to see exactly how our guys operated in that situation," said Jets coach Aaron Glenn, adding that he could've helped the players with better defensive calls.

 It was another uneven day for the Jets, who had some hiccups in their own two-minute drive -- a drop by RB Braelon Allen , a holding call on RT Armand Membou and a false start. QB Geno Smith completed only two of seven passes on the drive, which ended with a missed field goal (61 yards) by Jason Sanders .

 "I felt like we could've made a few more plays," Smith said.

 The same could be said of the entire two-day experience. The Bucs, a playoff team in three of Todd Bowles' four seasons as coach, proved themselves the superior team.

 Silver lining for the Jets: This was a learning experience, a not-so-subtle reminder they still have a lot of…

title: 2026 Seattle Seahawks training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Seahawks training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Packers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 Sources: Seahawks still plan on signing Terrion Arnold 
 Cooper Kupp's latest route? Opening a new coffee shop 
 Seahawks, Witherspoon reach extension: 4 years, $132M, sources say 
 Seahawks' DeMarcus Lawrence confirms 2026 season his last 
 Facing charges, Terrion Arnold set to join Seahawks 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 
 There are so many ways in which Mike Macdonald coaches the Seahawks differently from his predecessor, and this week is about to bring another example.

 Whereas Pete Carroll was staunchly against joint practices -- he never held one in 14 seasons in Seattle -- Macdonald is a proponent. It's why the Seahawks will head to Nashville on Thursday to practice against the Tennessee Titans on Friday, two days before their preseason game at Nissan Stadium.

 The Seahawks held joint practices in each of Macdonald's first two seasons -- in Nashville in 2024 and against the Packers in Green Bay last summer.

 Macdonald sees a best-of-all-worlds appeal in getting reps against another team in the controlled setting of a practice, where the two sides can simulate certain situations, and where the quarterbacks are not to be touched. Teams can also run plays that they wouldn't call in preseason games lest they put them on film for the rest of the league to see.

 "It's a lot of intentional reps," safety Julian Love said. "You're not just going through a game setting. You're doing one-on-ones against these guys, you're doing third-down period, certain concept periods against them, but you're going full go. It's cool where you get intentional work. It's always good to see other [starters] just so you can read and react. Me as a DB, it's nice when you can play a ball in a different setting against different people, get some different tendencies.

 "We're going to value it. The whole team is going to really take advantage of these reps because they're important."

 Fights are a common occurrence in joint practices. That's likely one reason the Seahawks have opted for just a single session after doing two of them against the Titans in 2024. Punches flew even in their lone practice against the Packers. 

 When things aren't getting out of hand on the field, another benefit of joint practices is the opportunity they provide for team bonding.

 "Two years ago in Tennessee, last year in Green Bay, it was the first time everyone let their hair down and enjoyed hanging out with each other," Love said. "Traveling with the team is always fun. We love traveling with each other just because it's a time where guys can just get a break and be with each other. Playing against another team in that kind of competitive space is fun. Then we go out to dinner, do the rookie [talent] show, all that stuff is a lot of fun. I know a lot of the guys are really excited about it."

 More observations: 

 
 RB Jadarian Price practiced for a second straight day. Seattle's top pick didn't practice for over a week due to what Macdonald called lower-body soreness. 
 RB Emanuel Wilson remains sidelined for undisclosed reasons. 
 CB Josh Jobe made the play of the day when he jumped in front of Rashid Shaheed and intercepted a short throw from Sam Darnold for what likely would have been a pick-six in a game. Darnold and Shaheed connected earlier on a deep throw that traveled about 45 yards in the air. 
 Backup G Bryce Cabeldue left practice with an apparent neck/head injury. 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 16 
 One lesser-known player who's making his best case for a job with the Seahawks in 2026 is Montorie Foster Jr . The second-year receiver continued his strong summer with a touchdown catch in Seattle's preseason opener, a 17-7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys .

 This time last year, he was unsigned and thinking about giving up football.

 Foster joined the Seahawks as an undrafted free agent in 2025. But after he hurt his hamstring and was waived with an injury designation in early August, he returned home to Cleveland and began looking for regular jobs. He got his real estate license and even worked as a substitute teacher at St. Edward High School, his alma mater.

 "I had a Latin class," he said postgame. "I don't know any Latin, at all."

 But Foster appears to know what "carpe diem" means, because he's grabbing a hold of his latest opportunity with Seattle. The Seahawks brought him back to their practice squad in December, signed him to a futures deal after the Super Bowl and are now seeing him make a serious push to stick around in some capacity.

 "Every time I play, I play to a standard and it don't matter if I'm playing good or bad, my standard is my standard," he said. "I go out there every day and just try to put my best foot forward every day and put forth the effort, go block, do the little things and let everything else take care of itself."

 Foster makes at least one play virtually every day. On Saturday, he almost made two. After catching a 5-yard touchdown from Drew Lock to cap Seattle's opening drive, he got open on a go route down the sideline for what would have been another score had Lock not overthrown him.

 "The journey he's been on from the previous year until now, man, he's light-years away from where he was, and he's been fantastic for us," Lock said. "He makes great plays. Explosive with the ball in his hand. Reliable. He's going to catch the ball. Yeah, nothing but confidence for him."

 It'll be tough for Foster to make Seattle's 53-man roster. Tory Horton is healthy and one of the league's more overqualified No. 4 receivers behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba , Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed . The Seahawks gave Jake Bobo a two-year, $5.5 million deal, so he's making the team. Even if they keep a sixth receiver, Cody White would also be in play for that spot.

 But based on the frequency with which he's made plays, Foster looks like someone the Seahawks would at least like to keep on their practice squad, if they can get him there. Whether it's in Seattle or elsewhere, he should be on an NFL team this fall and not at the front of a Latin class.

 "It means everything," Foster said of his opportunity. "I was back at home for 16 weeks and it was tough. There were times where I wanted to give up and get a regular job. But I stayed at it. My dad told me that cream always rises to the top and to just stay faithful. I just kept working, and now I'm here today."

 More observations: 

 
 Mike Macdonald was less than pleased with how the Seahawks played against Dallas, saying their operation and the way they finished plays was not up to their standard. "That's the most people I've ever seen at a preseason game," he said of the fans at Lumen Field. "We owe them a better performance, to say the least."

title: 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from 49ers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at 49ers camp. What does  Mike Evans  look like as a top receiver on the 49ers? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the 49ers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from 49ers' camp 
 
 Shanahan dismisses idea RB McCaffrey sitting out for new deal 
 Can the 49ers depend on rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling? 
 49ers' Ricky Pearsall has knee surgery, targets 9-month recovery 
 How the 49ers' defense looks different under Raheem Morris 
 Kyle Shanahan nears full strength, plans to coach preseason opener 
 Kittle eyes opener in Australia 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 
 EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- The 49ers' offense largely had its way with the Titans in a joint practice last week, but that was far from the case against the Chargers.

 The unit started well, as rookie running back Kaelon Black broke some big runs early. But the Chargers settled in for the second half and made life hard on QB Brock Purdy & Co. in the move-the-ball, two-minute and red zone periods.

 Chargers linebacker  Del'Shawn Phillips  even picked off a Purdy pass intended for tight end  Luke Farrell when safety  Derwin James Jr . got his hand in the way and tipped it to him.

 All in all, it wasn't the most encouraging outing against another team that should be a playoff contender this season.

 "Obviously, there was some good stuff, some stuff we need to work on, but I just feel like they came out with a little more of a chip on their shoulder," Purdy said.

 More observations: 

 
 The 49ers and Chargers were all about their business with no notable skirmishes. That's unusual for a joint practice, and it led to Shanahan delivering the funniest line of the day as he poked fun at Robert Saleh, the Titans' coach and his good friend. Asked if there was a reason for the lack of fighting, Shanahan joked, "No, [the Chargers'] head coach has more discipline than Tennessee's." 
 Black was one of three 49ers to return to practice Tuesday, joining receiver  Demarcus Robinson (who only missed Sunday) and defensive lineman  Keion White . White and Black had been dealing with adductor injuries, though White did not finish the session. 
 Defensive tackle  C.J. West did not practice because of a concussion, which makes him the fifth player in this camp to have suffered a head injury. Defensive lineman  Titus Leo also had a concussion and was waived/injured Tuesday as the team brought back defensive tackle  Evan Anderson . 
 The competition for the backup running back job behind Christian McCaffrey has been difficult to handicap because of injuries to all of the primary contenders for that job. But Black picked up where he left off before his injury. He broke a long, possible touchdown run down the left side early in the session and clearly has the freshest legs of the bunch. 
 Chargers OLB  Tuli Tuipulotu  gave the Niners fits, particularly in the run game where he had at least three run stuffs. 
 WR  Mike Evans , who returned from a tight quad last week, took part in most of Tuesday's practice but stopped before the final periods. He initially had his left foot wrapped in ice before watching the end of the session with that ice pack relocated to his left quad. 
 
 
 

 Sunday, Aug. 16 
 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa hasn't practiced since Aug. 3. In fact, Bosa hadn't been spotted on the practice field doing work on the side since then. Until Sunday.

 Though Bosa, who has been battling soreness and tendinitis as he recovers from a torn ACL, did not return to practice, he went through an extensive workout on a side field. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan said Tuesday that Bosa is dealing with "a pretty normal thing with ACLs," but given Bosa's injury history and that he was practicing before the soreness, it seemed to be a setback.

 "We have to be smart here from week to week," Shanahan said. "But no concerns about him."

 Though there are still hurdles to clear before Bosa returns to practice, Sunday was, at minimum, a notable step forward.

 More observations: 

 
 Three 49ers were added to the nonparticipant list Sunday: G Dominick Puni is in concussion protocol, defensive tackle Gracen Halton has an ankle injury and WR Demarcus Robinson missed the session for undisclosed reasons. 
 DT C.J. West and DE Titus Leo were hurt on back-to-back plays during a team drill. Both limped to the locker room and did not return. 
 WR  Deebo Samuel Sr . and WR Jacob Cowing were also shaken up at various points but returned and finished the session. 
 QB Kurtis Rourke did not practice again after he left last week's preseason opener because of breathing trouble. It's unclear what his injury is, but OC Klay Kubiak indicated that Rourke won't be out long. 
 With Puni out, Robert Jones worked at right guard as Jones, Connor Colby and Carver Willis continue to push for the starting left guard job. 
 Undrafted rookie DT James Thompson Jr . has been an under-the-radar surprise in camp and got some extra looks with the starters after West went down. 
 CB Renardo Green took issue with an official after he was whistled for a couple of penalties in red zone work. He got a flag for defensive pass interference then one for defensive holding. When he successfully defended a third pass thrown his way, he asked the official why he didn't throw a third flag. 
 Cowing had, perhaps, the best play of the day, laying out for a deep ball down the middle from QB Brock Purdy for the catch and a big gain. 
 
 

 Who is the 49ers' top performer so far at camp? 
 QB Brock Purdy . There are others deserving of mention here, but this has been Purdy's best and most consistent training camp despite working with a constantly changing supporting cast. No matter who has been at running back or receiver, Purdy has found ways to move the offense in nearly every practice. He has been particularly sharp when pushing the ball downfield for big plays. If healthy, he looks poised for a big year.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Where's the pass rush coming from? The Niners were last in the NFL in sacks (20) and 31st in pressures (157) in 2025. In the offseason, they traded for defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa ; they used draft picks on edge Romello Height and defensive tackle Gracen Halton . All three should help, but with defensive ends Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams not yet back from ACL surgeries, the exhibition slate will be the time for others to step forward and carve out roles.

 
 Saturday, Aug. 15 
 For the 49ers offense, there aren't many obviously available spots in the starting lineup. The exception comes at left guard where the competition is growing larger rather than narrowing as the season approaches.

 In Saturday's practice, the Niners added rookie Carver Willis to the mix after Connor Colby and Robert Jones have spent the first few weeks of camp rotating with the starting unit. Colby went first but in the next set of snaps, it was Willis working next to left tackle Trent Williams . Nobody has separated there so far and it was tough sledding blocking DT Osa Odighizuwa in this session, which means any formal decision is going to take some time.

 "Those guys are competing," Williams said. "It's a three-man race, so may the best man win, but they're all playing their butts off. Carver is the youngest and he got a little more to learn, but he has a high ceiling, a lot of potential. So just can't wait to see how he develops."
